nodes.text: Exertional buttock claudication with absent femoral pulses localizes disease to the aortoiliac segment.
**Intact pulses with relief on lumbar flexion:** evaluate for lumbar spinal stenosis.
Measure resting ABI.
**ABI ≤ 0.90:** confirm PAD and start structured exercise, high-intensity statin, aspirin or clopidogrel, and smoking cessation.
**Disabling claudication despite medical therapy and exercise:** obtain duplex or CT angiography to plan revascularization.
**Ischemic rest pain or tissue loss:** urgently refer for revascularization.

n-12-n12b1-q002.trap: Long smoking history makes lung cancer tempting, but cardiovascular mortality is higher.

algorithm.title: Cardiovascular risk reduction in postmenopausal women

nodes.text: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in postmenopausal women.
Use PREVENT-ASCVD to estimate primary prevention risk and address smoking, diet, activity, and blood pressure.
**LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL:** start a high-intensity statin without calculating risk.
**PREVENT-ASCVD risk ≥5% with LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL:** discuss at least moderate-intensity statin therapy.
**Confirmed BP ≥140/90 mm Hg:** start antihypertensive therapy with lifestyle changes.
**BP 130–139/80–89 mm Hg with elevated cardiovascular risk:** consider drug therapy based on comorbidities and predicted risk.

nodes.text: Sudden pleuritic chest pain + unilateral diminished breath sounds: assess stability
**Tension pneumothorax (hypotension, tracheal shift):** emergent needle thoracostomy
Obtain upright chest radiograph
**Small pneumothorax (< 2 cm) + asymptomatic:** supplemental oxygen + observation
**Large pneumothorax (>= 2 cm) or symptomatic hypoxia:** insert tube thoracostomy
Connect thoracostomy tube to water-seal drainage and repeat radiograph
**Persistent air leak > 48 hours:** perform video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery

nodes.text: Isolated thrombocytopenia + mucosal bleeding: review peripheral blood smear
**Schistocytes present:** evaluate for thrombotic microangiopathy or DIC
Rule out secondary causes (HIV, hepatitis C virus, systemic lupus erythematosus)
**Platelets < 30,000/mm³ or active bleeding:** administer oral prednisone or IVIG
**Life-threatening hemorrhage:** platelet transfusion + IVIG + high-dose methylprednisolone
Avoid NSAIDs, antiplatelet agents, and contact sports
**Relapsed or chronic ITP:** initiate thrombopoietin receptor agonists or rituximab

nodes.text: Dyspnea with elevated JVP, bilateral crackles, and an S3 suggests decompensated heart failure.
Obtain ECG, chest x-ray, BNP, and echocardiography to characterize heart failure and identify precipitants.
**Pulmonary or systemic congestion:** give IV furosemide.
**Hypertensive pulmonary edema:** add IV nitroglycerin.
**Hypotension with end-organ hypoperfusion:** give norepinephrine and consider dobutamine for low output.
**EF ≤40% after stabilization:** initiate sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, spironolactone if eligible, and dapagliflozin.

algorithm.title: Delivery room management of periviable birth

nodes.text: Extremely preterm delivery: assess gestational age and signs of viability
**≥ 25 weeks:** full neonatal resuscitation
**22–24 weeks:** resuscitation individualized after parental counseling
**< 22 weeks, fused eyelids, weight < 500 g, no response:** nonviable
Discontinue resuscitative efforts
Comfort care: warm, wrap, allow parents to hold
Family bereavement support

Obtain endoscopic sinus aspirate for culture.
Start IV cefepime for suspected hospital-acquired gram-negative infection and tailor therapy to cultures.
**Persistent fever and purulence despite tube removal and active antibiotics:** consult ENT for endoscopic drainage.

nodes.text: Recognize postpartum depression with persistent depressed mood, flat affect, and functional impairment beyond transient postpartum blues.
Assess suicidality, infant safety, and past mania or hypomania.
Start an SSRI such as sertraline for moderate to severe unipolar postpartum depression.
**Intent to harm the infant:** arrange supervised infant care and emergency psychiatric assessment.
**Delusions, hallucinations, or disorganization:** protect the infant and admit for antipsychotic treatment.
**Catatonia, severe suicidality, or inadequate response to treatment:** obtain urgent psychiatric assessment for ECT.
Offer CBT or interpersonal psychotherapy and arrange close follow-up.

nodes.text: Preeclampsia with severe features: BP ≥ 160/110, renal dysfunction, visual symptoms
Uteroplacental vasculopathy → placental abruption is the key labor complication
IV magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis
IV labetalol, hydralazine, or immediate-release nifedipine for BP ≥ 160/110
**≥ 34 weeks:** delivery after stabilization
**< 34 weeks, stable mother and fetus:** betamethasone; expectant management
**Vaginal bleeding, painful rigid uterus, fetal distress:** abruption; urgent delivery
Continue magnesium through 24 hours postpartum

Diagnostic confirmation: targeted genetic testing for HTT gene CAG trinucleotide expansion
**> 39 CAG repeats:** fully penetrant Huntington disease
**36-39 CAG repeats:** reduced penetrance Huntington disease
Brain MRI: bilateral caudate nucleus and putamen atrophy with ventricular enlargement
Manage chorea: VMAT2 inhibitors (tetrabenazine, deutetrabenazine) or atypical antipsychotics
Provide pre-test genetic counseling for at-risk family members

algorithm.title: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) evaluation and management

nodes.text: Recognize marked leukocytosis with full myeloid spectrum (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, neutrophils)
Differentiate CML (low LAP score, basophilia) from leukemoid reaction (high LAP score)

Bone marrow biopsy: assess blast percentage to stage disease (chronic vs accelerated vs blast phase)
**Chronic phase (< 10% blasts):** initiate tyrosine kinase inhibitor (imatinib, dasatinib, or nilotinib)
**Accelerated or blast phase (> 20% blasts):** high-intensity chemo + allogeneic stem cell transplant
Monitor molecular response with quantitative BCR-ABL1 transcripts every 3 months

algorithm.title: Pediatric febrile urinary tract infection evaluation

nodes.text: Obtain renal and bladder ultrasound (RBUS) for first febrile UTI in children

Grade vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) from grade I to grade V based on VCUG findings
**High-grade reflux (grades III-V):** daily antibiotic prophylaxis or ureteral reimplantation
Order DMSA renal scintigraphy if needed to evaluate permanent renal cortical scarring

**Starting nutritional refeeding:** monitor phosphate, potassium, magnesium

algorithm.title: Neonatal jaundice in first 24 hours: ABO incompatibility

nodes.text: Recognize pathologic jaundice: onset within first 24 hours of life
Differential: ABO incompatibility, Rh isoimmunization, G6PD deficiency, spherocytosis, sepsis

Initiate intensive phototherapy based on hour-specific bilirubin nomogram
**Rapidly rising bilirubin (> 0.5 mg/dL/hr) or failure of phototherapy:** IV immunoglobulin (IVIG)
**Bilirubin reaches exchange transfusion threshold:** urgent double-volume exchange transfusion

algorithm.title: Attributable risk calculation in cohort studies

nodes.text: Prospective cohort study: identify incidence of disease in exposed and unexposed groups
Calculate risk in exposed group: Ie = a / (a + b)
Calculate baseline risk in unexposed group: Iu = c / (c + d)
Calculate attributable risk: AR = Ie - Iu
**Interpret AR:** excess disease incidence directly attributable to the exposure
**Calculate attributable risk percent:** ARP = (Ie - Iu) / Ie

algorithm.title: Aortic valve stenosis evaluation and staging

nodes.text: Harsh crescendo-decrescendo murmur at the base with a soft A2 suggests aortic stenosis.
Use Doppler echocardiography to measure valve area, gradient, and peak velocity.
**Exertional dyspnea, angina, or syncope with peak velocity ≥4 m/s or mean gradient ≥40 mm Hg:** refer for valve replacement.
**Older patient or high surgical risk with suitable anatomy:** consider transcatheter valve replacement.
**Younger patient with low surgical risk and long life expectancy:** favor surgical valve replacement.
**Severe stenosis without symptoms and preserved LV function:** arrange close surveillance and reassess for exercise-induced symptoms.
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe stenosis.

algorithm.title: Acute valvular destruction in infective endocarditis

nodes.text: Infective endocarditis patient developing acute pulmonary edema + new murmurs: suspect valve rupture
Perform emergent transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography
**Severe acute regurgitation with heart failure:** consult cardiac surgery for urgent replacement
Administer intravenous vasodilators and diuretics for pulmonary congestion if stable
**Cardiogenic shock present:** initiate inotropes and avoid balloon pump in aortic regurgitation
Continue targeted bactericidal intravenous antibiotic therapy

nodes.text: Asthma with brown mucus plugs, fleeting infiltrates, and central bronchiectasis suggests allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis.
Expect Aspergillus fumigatus sensitization; measure Aspergillus-specific IgE and total IgE.
**Aspergillus sensitization and total IgE ≥500 IU/mL:** assess eosinophilia, Aspergillus IgG, and characteristic imaging to confirm ABPA.
**New symptomatic ABPA:** treat with oral prednisolone or itraconazole.
**Recurrent ABPA exacerbations:** combine prednisolone and itraconazole.
**Relapse when tapering therapy despite antifungal treatment:** consider omalizumab with pulmonary or allergy consultation.

**Fever with delayed access to care:** take the prescribed rescue antibiotic and seek emergency assessment immediately.
**Fever on presentation:** obtain blood cultures without delaying empiric IV ceftriaxone.

algorithm.title: Preconception and pregnancy care in cystic fibrosis

nodes.text: Review preconception pulmonary function (FEV1) and baseline nutrition
Optimize nutritional status prior to and throughout pregnancy
**BMI < 22 kg/m2 or suboptimal weight gain:** high-calorie diet + enteral feeds + pancreatic enzymes
Screen for cystic fibrosis-related diabetes with 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test
**Elevated fasting or postprandial glucose:** start subcutaneous insulin
Continue chest physiotherapy + inhaled mucolytics + inhaled bronchodilators
**Acute pulmonary exacerbation:** targeted antipseudomonal IV antibiotics
Screen partner for CFTR mutations to assess fetal cystic fibrosis risk

n-12-q085.boardCall: Infant with acute bacterial meningitis -> Sensorineural hearing loss
n-12-q085.hinge: Sensorineural hearing loss is the single most common long-term sequela of acute bacterial meningitis.
n-12-q085.trap: Subdural effusions occur frequently in infants with H influenzae, but usually resolve spontaneously.

A.clue: Focal spinal or intracranial collection from direct extension
A.fit: Not here: localized suppurative collection rather than generalized meningeal sequela
A.tempting: bacterial spreading can cause localized parameningeal pus collections

B.clue: Suppurative cochlear inflammation causing permanent auditory deficit
B.fit: Here: acute bacterial meningitis carries highest long-term risk of sensorineural hearing loss

C.fit: Not here: obstructive hydrocephalus occurs far less frequently than auditory impairment

E.fit: Not here: common transient finding that typically resolves spontaneously without deficits
E.tempting: common transient finding on neuroimaging in infant meningitis

algorithm.title: Acute bacterial meningitis in infants: complications and management

nodes.text: Bacterial meningitis can cause permanent sensorineural hearing loss through cochlear inflammation.
Obtain blood cultures and CSF when safe; avoid delaying antibiotics for lumbar puncture.
**Neonate under 28 days:** use IV ampicillin plus cefotaxime.
**Older infant with community-acquired bacterial meningitis:** use IV ceftriaxone plus vancomycin pending cultures.
Arrange formal audiology after stabilization, ideally before discharge, and follow neurologic development.
**Confirmed severe or profound sensorineural hearing loss:** refer promptly for cochlear implant evaluation.

Pelvic ultrasound: assess presence of uterus and ovaries

**FSH elevated (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism):** order karyotype analysis
**FSH low or normal:** brain MRI to evaluate hypothalamic-pituitary lesions
**Uterus absent:** order karyotype + serum testosterone (Müllerian agenesis vs androgen insensitivity)
**Turner syndrome (45,X):** echocardiogram + renal ultrasound + hormone replacement

nodes.text: Macroglossia, large fontanels, and developmental delay after missed newborn screening suggest congenital hypothyroidism.
Obtain serum TSH and free T4 to confirm the diagnosis.
**High TSH with low free T4:** start oral levothyroxine promptly to prevent irreversible neurodevelopmental injury.
**Low free T4 with low or normal TSH:** evaluate central hypothyroidism and assess cortisol before replacement.
Recheck thyroid function within one to two weeks after starting treatment.
**TSH remains elevated on treatment:** check administration and adherence, then titrate levothyroxine using age-specific targets.

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

acute-respiratory-failure.name: Acute respiratory failure
acute-respiratory-failure.scope: Hypoxemic respiratory failure (type 1), hypercapnic respiratory failure (type 2), noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (BiPAP/CPAP), indications for invasive mechanical ventilation
acute-respiratory-failure.core: Acute inability to maintain oxygenation or ventilation demands simultaneous cause treatment and escalating respiratory support, guided by work of breathing and airway safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pneumonia, pulmonary edema, ARDS, PE → oxygenation failure
COPD, neuromuscular weakness, obesity hypoventilation, sedatives → ventilation failure; overlap common

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachypnea, accessory-muscle use, hypoxemia, diaphoresis; hypercapnia may cause headache, somnolence, asterixis
★ **Exhaustion, declining consciousness, silent chest, paradoxical breathing** → impending respiratory arrest
Normal saturation on supplemental oxygen does not exclude dangerous CO₂ retention

rows.label: Pathophys
items: V/Q mismatch, shunt, or diffusion impairment lowers PaO₂; shunt may resist oxygen alone
Inadequate alveolar ventilation raises PaCO₂; abrupt rise causes respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pulse oximetry + ABG** when severe distress, hypercapnia concern, or escalating support
Chest radiograph, ECG, bedside lung/cardiac ultrasound; infection/PE testing follows clinical context
Trend pH, gases, respiratory rate, mentation and effort; do not wait for an extreme number
Chronic compensated hypercapnia has elevated bicarbonate; pH decline identifies acute deterioration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oxygen immediately**, treat cause; target SpO₂ 88–92% with CO₂-retention risk, usually 92–96% otherwise
Hypoxemic failure needing more than conventional oxygen → high-flow nasal cannula, close reassessment
★ Awake cooperative COPD + respiratory acidosis → **BiPAP**; cardiogenic edema → CPAP/BiPAP plus diuresis/nitrates
★ **Intubate** for airway failure, refractory hypoxemia, shock, arrest, exhaustion, or worsening despite noninvasive support
Avoid NIV with vomiting, unprotected airway, copious secretions, major facial trauma; reassess within 1–2 h

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxic brain injury, arrhythmia, multiorgan failure; delayed intubation worsens outcome
Positive pressure → hypotension/barotrauma; invasive ventilation → pneumonia and ventilator-induced lung injury
Ventilated ARDS: low tidal volume using predicted body weight, limited plateau pressure; prone if severe

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, respiratory vaccination, disease control, cautious sedatives, aspiration precautions
High-risk extubation patients may benefit from planned NIV rather than rescue after deterioration
Awake, stable, low ventilator support → **spontaneous breathing trial** to wean, before tracheostomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metabolic acidosis: compensatory tachypnea with low CO₂
Panic hyperventilation: respiratory alkalosis without sustained gas-exchange failure

table.title: Gas-exchange classification; room air when feasible

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Respiratory exposure, daycare contacts, impaired drainage from allergic inflammation
Immunocompromise, recent antibiotics, or hospitalization increases resistant-organism risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, reduced smell, maxillary tenderness; colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection
★ Orbital swelling, painful eye movement, reduced vision, severe headache → **complicated infection**
Well febrile child, URI symptoms, clear lungs, good perfusion: soft flow murmur innocent, not VSD

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral mucosal edema blocks sinus drainage; secondary infection commonly pneumococcus, H influenzae, or Moraxella

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; uncomplicated illness needs neither sinus radiographs nor CT
Persistent, severe, or biphasic course identifies bacterial cases; fever alone is insufficient
Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**, oral pseudoephedrine (not young children); no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

table.title: Bacterial patterns
rows: Initial improvement → new fever or worsening symptoms

adjustment-disorder.name: Adjustment disorder
adjustment-disorder.scope: Identifiable psychosocial stressor within 3 months, marked distress or functional impairment, resolution within 6 months, psychotherapy
adjustment-disorder.core: Disproportionate distress or functional impairment beginning within 3 months of an identifiable stressor, without meeting criteria for another disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Relationship loss, illness, job loss, relocation, school difficulty; limited social support or coping resources
Prior psychiatric illness, ongoing adversity, cumulative stress; assess cultural context and expected responses

rows.label: Clues
items: Anxiety, depressed mood, mixed emotions, or conduct disturbance linked temporally to the event
★ Symptoms resolve within **6 months after stressor/consequences end**; may persist with ongoing stress
Sleep difficulty, worry, withdrawal, reduced performance; impairment exceeds an expected adaptive response

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress-related maladaptive coping and emotional dysregulation; no required traumatic exposure or unique biomarker

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical chronology** plus functional assessment; clarify symptoms before and after the stressor
★ Screen **suicidality**, substance use, mania, psychosis; investigate medical causes suggested by history
Full major-depressive syndrome takes precedence even when triggered by a clear life event
Reassess persistence, escalating severity, or loss of temporal connection; diagnosis may change over time

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Brief psychotherapy**, problem solving, CBT, coping skills; strengthen support and reduce modifiable stress
Address sleep routines, daily structure, school/work accommodations and practical resources
Medication usually unnecessary; severe acute anxiety/insomnia → brief **benzodiazepine** (older exams); SSRIs take weeks
Suicidal intent, inability to maintain safety, or severe deterioration → urgent psychiatric assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Self-harm, suicide risk, substance misuse, occupational or academic decline
Persistent symptoms may evolve into major depression, anxiety disorder, or another defined condition

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early transition support, coping skills, follow-up until recovery; involve trusted supports with consent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Major depression: ≥2 weeks, ≥5 symptoms including depressed mood/anhedonia
PTSD/acute stress disorder: qualifying trauma plus intrusion/avoidance; PTSD >1 month, acute stress 3 days–1 month
Normal grief: fluctuating loss-focused sadness with preserved self-worth and adaptive function
GAD: ≥6 months of multi-domain worry, not tied to one recent stressor

adjustment-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR teaching.

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.name: Adolescent confidentiality and care
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.scope: Confidentiality principles, exceptions to parental notification, parental requests for drug testing, encouraging family involvement
adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.core: Provide adolescents private, developmentally appropriate care; explain confidentiality and its safety limits before sensitive questions.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality supports honest disclosure; consent authority and parental access vary by jurisdiction
Assent: involve the adolescent even when guardian permission remains necessary
Contraception: minors generally consent confidentially; no parental notice or pelvic exam required

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview alone** for sexual health, substance use, mood, violence, and safety
★ Explain permitted confidential services; protect portals, billing, and result notifications
Encourage trusted-adult involvement; never require disclosure for legally confidential services

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Parental request for **drug testing** → discuss concern, interview teen; avoid covert testing
Do not promise absolute secrecy or automatically send sensitive findings to parents
Do not breach for experimental substance use without impairment → counsel, schedule **follow-up visit**

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Imminent danger, suspected **abuse/neglect/exploitation** → protective disclosure and reporting
Emergency treatment when delay risks serious harm; involve guardians when feasible
Emancipated minors generally self-consent; pregnancy alone does not universally confer emancipation

rows.label: Traps
items: Minor consent varies: STI, contraception, pregnancy, mental health, substance; **elective surgery** → parents
Mandatory reporting thresholds for consensual sexual activity depend on ages and local law
Disclose minimum necessary information; explain safety-driven disclosure to adolescent whenever feasible

adolescent-confidentiality-and-care.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; jurisdiction-specific consent/reporting law must be verified locally.

adolescent-preventive-care.name: Adolescent preventive care
adolescent-preventive-care.scope: Leading causes of death, injury prevention, HEADSS psychosocial screening, adolescent screening tests
adolescent-preventive-care.core: Private, developmentally appropriate preventive visits identify injury risk, mental illness, substance use, sexual health needs, and barriers to healthy development.

rows.label: Who
items: All adolescents annually; explain confidentiality and safety exceptions, with some time alone
Leading death cause: **unintentional injury**, then suicide, homicide; risk varies by age and population

rows.label: Start/stop
items: HEADSS: Home, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/depression; include strengths and safety
★ Annual **depression and suicide-risk screening from 12**; assess younger patients when concerned
HIV once during adolescence, repeat with ongoing risk; lipids once at 17–21 years

rows.label: Test
items: ★ BP, BMI, development; **chlamydia/gonorrhea annually** for sexually active females <25
Exposure-site STI testing for MSM; syphilis/TB/anemia testing by risk
Assess sleep, nutrition, eating disorders, substances/vaping, violence, school, sexual coercion

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Positive suicide screen → **brief safety assessment**, urgent evaluation for imminent risk
Post-menarche → pregnancy/STI prevention, contraception; treat STIs; substance-use counseling; accessible follow-up
Counsel seat belts, helmets, no impaired/distracted driving; secure firearms unloaded and locked

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No routine Pap before 21**, even with sexual activity; STI screening uses separate tests
Depression screening alone misses some suicide risk; ask directly about thoughts and plans
Early post-menarche: irregular cycles normal, no hormone testing; update HPV, MenACWY, Tdap

adrenal-insufficiency.name: Adrenal insufficiency
adrenal-insufficiency.scope: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), secondary adrenal insufficiency, cosyntropin stimulation test, morning serum cortisol, hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement, adrenal crisis
adrenal-insufficiency.core: Weight loss, fatigue, orthostasis, and hyponatremia, or unexplained pressor-resistant shock after illness or interruption of glucocorticoids.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Primary: autoimmune destruction, TB, bilateral hemorrhage, metastases; associated autoimmune thyroid disease
★ Secondary: **prolonged glucocorticoids**, pituitary disease/surgery/apoplexy; abrupt withdrawal risks crisis
Crisis triggers: infection, trauma, surgery, missed replacement, vomiting

rows.label: Clues
items: Anorexia, abdominal pain, nausea, weakness; hypoglycemia, eosinophilia
Crisis: fever, confusion, severe volume depletion; symptoms may worsen rapidly during intercurrent illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortisol deficiency reduces vascular catecholamine response and increases ADH
Primary gland failure removes mineralocorticoids; secondary disease retains renin–angiotensin-driven aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **8 AM cortisol + ACTH**; very low cortisol supports, clearly high values argue against insufficiency
★ Equivocal basal cortisol → **cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation**; inadequate assay-specific peak confirms impaired reserve
Traditional stimulated cutoff ≈18 µg/dL; newer assays may use ≈14–15; interpret laboratory standard
Primary → 21-hydroxylase antibodies, selected adrenal CT; secondary → pituitary evaluation/MRI
Recent pituitary injury may initially show normal cosyntropin response; clinical suspicion still matters

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crisis → draw blood if feasible, **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline**, dextrose for hypoglycemia
Do not wait for confirmatory results; treat precipitant and correct electrolytes carefully
Coexisting hypothyroidism → glucocorticoid replacement before levothyroxine to avoid decompensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated crisis → arrhythmia, circulatory collapse, death; chronic undertreatment → impaired function
Excess replacement → osteoporosis, diabetes, Cushingoid features

rows.label: Prevention
items: Stress-dose plan, emergency injectable hydrocortisone, medical alert ID; taper prolonged systemic steroids
Vomiting prevents absorption → parenteral replacement and urgent evaluation; teach sick-day plans to caregivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: SIADH: euvolemia, normal potassium and cortisol reserve
Sepsis: infection may coexist and trigger crisis
Hypothyroidism: bradycardia, cold intolerance, weight gain

table.title: Primary versus secondary
rows: Low/inappropriately normal ACTH; potassium usually normal

adrenal-insufficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching; cortisol cutoffs are assay dependent.

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

alcohol-use-disorder.name: Alcohol use disorder
alcohol-use-disorder.scope: Unhealthy alcohol use, CAGE and AUDIT screening, transaminitis (AST > ALT), motivational interviewing, naltrexone, acamprosate
alcohol-use-disorder.core: Compulsive alcohol use despite harm, impaired control, or physiologic dependence calls for nonjudgmental assessment and relapse-prevention treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, early initiation, trauma, depression, anxiety, social stress
Binge drinking and escalating tolerance; coexisting sedative use increases overdose risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Craving, failed attempts to cut down, role impairment, continued use despite consequences
AST:ALT ≥1.5–2, macrocytosis, elevated GGT support exposure but neither prove nor exclude disorder
★ Tremor, tachycardia, hallucinations, seizures after reduction → **withdrawal**, potentially fatal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic GABA enhancement/NMDA inhibition → compensatory adaptation; cessation unmasks CNS excitation
Mesolimbic reinforcement and stress circuitry sustain compulsive use and relapse

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screen adults using **AUDIT-C** or single-question heavy-use screen; positive result → fuller assessment
DSM-5: ≥2 of 11 criteria within 12 months; 2–3 mild, 4–5 moderate, ≥6 severe
CAGE: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener; ≥2 positive suggests problem use, misses early risky drinking
Assess suicidality, other drugs, liver disease, nutritional deficiency, pregnancy, withdrawal history
Depression or major life stressor → always ask about alcohol use

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: elicit goals, reflect ambivalence, agree achievable change; CBT and mutual support
Withdrawal → benzodiazepines; inpatient detoxification for severe history, unstable comorbidity, or unreliable support
Thiamine promptly for malnutrition/Wernicke risk; never delay emergency glucose for hypoglycemia
Disulfiram: selected supervised abstinence; avoid severe liver/cardiac disease; alcohol exposure causes aversive reaction

rows.label: Complications
items: Cirrhosis, pancreatitis, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, cancer, injuries, fetal alcohol effects
Wernicke encephalopathy → Korsakoff amnesia; depression and suicide risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Ongoing **relapse planning**, frequent follow-up, social support; abstinence for pregnancy or advanced liver disease
Assess hepatitis vaccination, nutrition, driving safety, medication interactions
Asymptomatic AST>ALT transaminitis (<500, unlike viral >1000) in daily drinker → reversible with abstinence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sedative withdrawal: similar autonomic excitation with benzodiazepine/barbiturate reduction
Hyperthyroidism: tremor/tachycardia without alcohol-linked time course

table.title: Relapse prevention
rows: Current opioids; acute hepatitis/severe hepatic failure

alcohol-use-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established screening and addiction-treatment principles.

allergic-rhinitis.name: Allergic rhinitis
allergic-rhinitis.scope: Seasonal and perennial rhinitis, bluish boggy turbinates, allergic shiners, intranasal glucocorticoids, oral antihistamines, allergen avoidance
allergic-rhinitis.core: Recurrent sneezing, nasal itching, and clear rhinorrhea after allergen exposure, often accompanied by itchy watery eyes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, asthma, eczema, family history; occupational allergen exposure
Seasonal: tree, grass, weed pollens; perennial: dust mites, pets, indoor molds

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pale bluish boggy turbinates**, allergic shiners, transverse nasal crease
Congestion, postnasal drip, mouth breathing; symptoms impair sleep, school, or work
Fever, purulent unilateral drainage, epistaxis, or focal pain warrants another explanation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links mast-cell IgE → histamine release; late eosinophilic inflammation sustains obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** from reproducible exposure pattern and examination
Uncertain diagnosis, persistent symptoms, or immunotherapy planning → skin-prick or serum allergen-specific IgE testing
Positive sensitization test requires matching exposure history; total IgE and imaging are not routine
Unilateral obstruction → inspect for foreign body, structural lesion, or mass

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent or congestion-dominant disease → **intranasal fluticasone**; direct spray away from septum
Mild intermittent disease → cetirizine or loratadine; intranasal azelastine offers rapid relief
Incomplete control → intranasal steroid + intranasal antihistamine; saline irrigation as adjunct
★ Refractory, confirmed sensitization → **allergen immunotherapy** with allergy specialist
Avoid sedating first-generation antihistamines in older adults; decongestant sprays >3 days → rebound congestion

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, reduced concentration, eustachian tube dysfunction, recurrent sinus symptoms
Intranasal steroid misuse → epistaxis; systemic decongestants → hypertension, tachycardia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Allergen reduction**: mattress encasements, hot-wash bedding, moisture control, exposure-directed pet avoidance
Close windows during high pollen periods; avoid tobacco smoke and personal irritants

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral URI: short course, malaise, possible fever
Nonallergic rhinitis: odor/temperature triggers, little itching, negative sensitization testing
Rhinitis medicamentosa: chronic topical vasoconstrictor use with rebound blockage

allergic-rhinitis.evidence: Not checked online; established rhinitis diagnostic and treatment principles.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.scope: Upper and lower motor neuron signs, bulbar symptoms, preserved sensation, EMG/NCS findings, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, riluzole, edaravone, end-of-life planning
amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.core: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs in multiple regions, usually with preserved sensation and sphincter function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Middle/older adulthood, male sex; mostly sporadic, minority familial
Family history of motor neuron disease or frontotemporal dementia supports inherited susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Atrophy, fasciculations + hyperreflexia/spasticity** within affected regions; asymmetric limb onset common
Bulbar disease: dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue wasting; pseudobulbar affect may accompany corticobulbar dysfunction
Orthopnea, morning headache, weak cough → ventilatory weakness; inward abdominal motion on inspiration → **diaphragmatic paralysis**
Ocular movement and sensation usually spared; some patients develop executive or behavioral impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Degeneration of corticospinal neurons and anterior horn/bulbar motor neurons; denervation spreads progressively

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical progression + EMG/NCS**: widespread **fibrillation potentials**, sharp waves, chronic denervation; sensory conduction normal
MRI brain/spine to exclude structural mimics; targeted B12, thyroid, CK, and other studies
Assess FVC, inspiratory strength, nocturnal gas exchange, swallow function, nutrition; no single definitive blood test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Riluzole** modestly prolongs survival; edaravone may slow functional decline in selected patients
★ **Noninvasive ventilation** for symptomatic respiratory weakness improves comfort and survival
Swallow/nutrition support; discuss gastrostomy before severe respiratory decline; cough-assist and secretion management
Baclofen for spasticity, communication devices, physical/occupational support; multidisciplinary specialty care
Early shared planning for ventilation, feeding, advance directives, hospice; discuss choices before communication declines

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure is usual terminal event; aspiration, malnutrition, falls, immobility
Depression, caregiver burden; frontotemporal impairment may affect decision-making capacity

rows.label: Prevention
items: No primary prevention; aspiration/fall precautions, vaccination, nutritional support, respiratory surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical myelopathy: sensory level, sphincter changes, compressive MRI lesion
Myasthenia gravis: fatigable ocular weakness, no UMN signs
Multifocal motor neuropathy: conduction block, IVIG response

amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis.evidence: Not checked online; established ALS diagnosis and supportive-treatment teaching.

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

ankle-and-foot-injuries.name: Ankle and foot injuries
ankle-and-foot-injuries.scope: Lateral ankle sprain, Ottawa ankle and foot rules, RICE therapy, functional rehabilitation, Achilles tendon rupture, plantar fasciitis, calcaneal apophysitis
ankle-and-foot-injuries.core: Mechanism, focal tenderness, weight-bearing ability, and tendon function distinguish ankle sprain from fracture and overuse foot disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Inversion while plantarflexed, prior sprain, poor balance → lateral ligament injury
Running/jumping, sudden training increase, tight calves, obesity; fluoroquinolones/steroids increase tendon rupture risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Lateral swelling after inversion → **anterior talofibular ligament** injury most likely
Pain above ankle with external rotation/squeeze → syndesmotic sprain; recovery slower
Focal bony pain, deformity, neurovascular changes, or inability to bear weight → fracture evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament overstretch → microtears or disruption; tendon degeneration predisposes rupture
Repeated loading damages soft tissue; tendon degeneration reduces tensile strength

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ankle pain + **posterior-edge/tip malleolar tenderness** → ankle radiographs
★ Midfoot pain + **navicular or fifth-metatarsal-base tenderness** → foot radiographs
Either region: inability to take four steps immediately and during evaluation also triggers corresponding radiographs
Examine skin, pulses, sensation; persistent focal pain despite normal films → reassess occult fracture

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sprain: **protection, ice, compression, elevation**, brief analgesia; early protected weight-bearing
Functional brace + range-of-motion, strength, proprioceptive rehabilitation; avoid prolonged routine immobilization
Displaced/open fracture or neurovascular compromise → urgent orthopedics; immobilize and keep non-weight-bearing

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic instability, recurrent sprains, osteochondral talar injury
Missed syndesmotic injury → prolonged disability; immobilization → stiffness, thrombosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Balance training and bracing** after prior sprain; gradual return when strength/function restored
Gradual training progression, supportive footwear, calf flexibility; avoid premature athletic return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lisfranc injury: plantar ecchymosis, midfoot instability; weight-bearing radiographs
Septic arthritis: fever, marked passive-motion pain; aspirate joint

table.title: Heel disorders
rows: Pop, weak plantarflexion, abnormal Thompson test
First-step morning pain; medial plantar heel
Active child; posterior heel squeeze tenderness

ankle-and-foot-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic decision rules and rehabilitation principles.

anorectal-disorders.name: Anorectal disorders
anorectal-disorders.scope: Anal fissure, internal and external hemorrhoids, anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, pruritus ani, topical vasodilators, fiber, sitz baths
anorectal-disorders.core: Anal pain, bleeding, swelling, or drainage requires inspection and focused examination; pain pattern distinguishes fissure, thrombosis, and infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constipation, straining, pregnancy, prolonged sitting; Crohn disease, diabetes, immunosuppression increase infection risk
Irritant soaps, moisture, fecal seepage contribute to pruritus ani

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pain out of proportion, fever, spreading erythema, crepitus** → evaluate necrotizing perineal infection urgently
Posterior midline fissure common; lateral/multiple fissures suggest Crohn disease, infection, or malignancy
Internal hemorrhoids lie above dentate line; prolapse may require manual reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fissure causes internal sphincter spasm and local ischemia; hemorrhoids represent enlarged vascular cushions
Cryptoglandular infection creates abscess; persistent epithelialized tract can become a fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspection first**, gentle DRE/anoscopy when tolerable; do not force painful fissure examination
Deep pain without visible lesion → CT/MRI for occult abscess; recurrent fistula → pelvic MRI
Rectal bleeding with anemia, weight loss, bowel change, or screening indication → colon evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fiber, fluids, stool softening, **sitz baths**; fissure → topical anesthetic, nitroglycerin or diltiazem
Refractory chronic fissure → botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy after continence-risk assessment
Internal hemorrhoids persisting despite conservative measures → rubber-band ligation; advanced prolapse → surgery
★ Abscess → **incision and drainage**; antibiotics added for cellulitis, systemic illness, or immunosuppression
Fistula → colorectal surgery; painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid within 72 hours → consider excision

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess recurrence, fistula, sepsis; sphincter injury → fecal incontinence
Chronic bleeding → iron deficiency; pruritus → excoriations and secondary infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid straining and prolonged toilet sitting; gentle cleansing, dry skin, barrier ointment for seepage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anal cancer: persistent irregular ulcer/mass or large wart-like lesion, biopsy required
Proctitis: urgency, tenesmus, mucous discharge
Pinworm: nocturnal itch, especially children; tape test

table.title: Local patterns
rows: Tearing defecation pain; bright blood on paper
Recurrent purulent drainage from external opening

anorectal-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established colorectal teaching.

anticholinergic-toxicity.name: Anticholinergic toxicity
anticholinergic-toxicity.scope: Antihistamines, tricyclic antidepressants, atropine, anticholinergic toxidrome, physostigmine
anticholinergic-toxicity.core: Delirium with mydriasis, dry flushed skin, hyperthermia, urinary retention, and reduced bowel sounds after muscarinic blockade.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diphenhydramine, first-generation antihistamines in OTC cold/sleep products, atropine, scopolamine, tricyclic antidepressants, toxic plants
Benztropine, trihexyphenidyl for parkinsonism/EPS; chlorpromazine and other low-potency antipsychotics
Older age, polypharmacy, accidental pediatric ingestion, intentional overdose; mixed toxidromes are common

rows.label: Clues
items: Agitation, hallucinations, picking at unseen objects, blurred vision, tachycardia
★ **Hot and dry**, rather than sweaty; severe poisoning causes seizures, coma, dysrhythmias
Palpable bladder, ileus; TCA exposure may add hypotension and conduction abnormalities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central/peripheral muscarinic antagonism; some causative drugs also block sodium channels
Absent sweating impairs heat dissipation; agitation further increases temperature
Muscarinic blockade → ↓**detrusor tone** → urinary retention; ↓gut motility → constipation/ileus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical toxidrome + ECG**; check QRS/QTc before considering reversal
Glucose, electrolytes, creatinine, CK; acetaminophen level for uncertain intentional ingestion
TCA markers: QRS >100 ms or terminal R in aVR signals sodium-channel toxicity
Drug screens do not establish severity; ECG and physiology drive treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway support, IV fluids, external cooling; **benzodiazepines** for agitation/seizures
**Stop offending drug** first; bladder catheter for retention; charcoal early only with protected airway
★ Pure severe antimuscarinic delirium → selected **physostigmine**, slow IV with continuous monitoring and expert supervision
Avoid physostigmine with suspected TCA/mixed cardiotoxic ingestion, QRS widening, significant conduction disease, or seizures
Sodium-channel blockade → **IV sodium bicarbonate**; avoid QT-prolonging antipsychotics in high-risk poisoning

rows.label: Complications
items: Rhabdomyolysis, AKI, aspiration, heat injury, ventricular arrhythmia, death
Physostigmine → bradycardia, seizures, asystole in unsuitable patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reduce anticholinergic burden, safe storage, avoid duplicate OTC sleep/cold products; assess intent after stabilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sympathomimetic toxicity: diaphoresis and active bowel sounds
Serotonin syndrome: clonus, hyperreflexia, diarrhea
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: lead-pipe rigidity, dopamine-blocker exposure

anticholinergic-toxicity.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency toxicology teaching.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

asplenia.name: Asplenia
asplenia.scope: Anatomic asplenia (splenectomy), functional asplenia (sickle cell), Howell-Jolly bodies, reactive thrombocytosis, encapsulated organism sepsis (Streptococcus pneumoniae), vaccination timing, antibiotic prophylaxis
asplenia.core: Absent or poorly functioning spleen impairs clearance of encapsulated organisms; fever can progress rapidly to fatal sepsis despite prior vaccination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Splenectomy for trauma/hematologic disease; functional loss with sickle cell disease; congenital absence
Sepsis risk greatest early after surgery and in children, but remains lifelong

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fever, rigors, malaise, vomiting, or rapid deterioration → **overwhelming postsplenectomy infection**
Pneumococcus especially important; also meningococcus, Hib; dog bites risk Capnocytophaga
Travel-associated malaria and Babesia can become unusually severe

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of splenic macrophage filtration and IgM memory B-cell function impairs opsonized-organism clearance
Reduced removal of erythrocyte inclusions and platelets explains characteristic blood findings

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Smear: **Howell–Jolly bodies**; reactive thrombocytosis after splenectomy; correlate with history/imaging
Febrile illness → cultures, CBC, lactate, source evaluation; do not delay antibiotics for results
Unexplained anemia/fever after tick exposure or travel → smear/PCR for intraerythrocytic parasites

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected sepsis → **immediate ceftriaxone**, add vancomycin for severe/resistant pneumococcal concern
Resuscitate and admit if ill; even initially mild fever requires urgent clinical evaluation
Standby oral antibiotic if immediate care inaccessible, followed by emergency evaluation; not a substitute for assessment
Daily penicillin/amoxicillin in young children, particularly sickle cell disease through at least age 5

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant bacteremia, meningitis, purpura fulminans, DIC, death
Postoperative thrombosis risk; isolated reactive platelet elevation does not automatically require antiplatelet treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Vaccinate **≥14 days before elective splenectomy**; after emergency surgery vaccinate once stable
Adult antibiotic prophylaxis individualized by postoperative period, immune status, and prior invasive infection
Medical alert ID, fever plan, influenza vaccination; bite counseling, travel precautions and malaria prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron deficiency: reactive thrombocytosis without splenic dysfunction
Hyposplenism: spleen present but impaired; similar infection precautions

table.title: Vaccine priorities: unvaccinated adults
rows: One dose if not previously vaccinated

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.name: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.scope: Leading cause of death, risk factors (smoking, diabetes, hypertension), ASCVD risk calculation, primary prevention (statins, aspirin)
atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.core: Plaque-driven coronary, cerebrovascular and peripheral arterial disease, a leading cause of death.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, high LDL, CKD, older age, premature family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional angina, transient focal neurologic deficits, or reproducible exertional calf pain
Often asymptomatic before first event

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Arterial LDL retention → inflammation and plaque; rupture or erosion → acute thrombosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ 2026 ACC/AHA: **PREVENT-ASCVD** for ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 mg/dL, no known ASCVD
Classic older questions: Pooled Cohort Equations; intermediate 7.5–<20%, high ≥20%
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium can refine risk

rows.label: Tx
items: Clinical ASCVD → high-intensity atorvastatin or rosuvastatin; antiplatelet therapy by vascular indication

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, ischemic stroke, limb ischemia, ischemic cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, exercise, Mediterranean-style diet, blood pressure and diabetes control
★ LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin without risk calculation
★ Age 40–75 with diabetes, CKD stage 3–4 or HIV → lipid-lowering therapy regardless of calculated risk
★ USPSTF aspirin: individualize ages 40–59 with ≥10% risk and low bleeding risk; avoid starting ≥60

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasospastic angina: rest episodes with transient ST elevation
Neurogenic claudication: relief with spinal flexion, preserved distal pulses

table.title: PREVENT 10-year risk and primary prevention
rows: Consider statin, especially with risk enhancers

atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease.evidence: Checked ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia guideline (2026) and USPSTF aspirin recommendation (2022).

autism-spectrum-disorder.name: Autism spectrum disorder
autism-spectrum-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria, social communication deficits, repetitive behaviors, M-CHAT screening, hearing evaluation, early behavioral therapy
autism-spectrum-disorder.core: Early developmental differences combining impaired reciprocal social communication with restricted, repetitive behavior or sensory interests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, affected sibling, male sex, certain genetic syndromes
Prematurity and older parental age increase risk; vaccines do not cause autism

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor eye contact, poor response to name, limited joint attention/pointing, absent pretend play, language delay, echolalia
Rigid routines, repetitive movements, narrow interests, unusual object attachment, sensory hyperreactivity or hyporeactivity
★ **Loss of acquired language or social skills** → prompt developmental and medical evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurodevelopmental differences affect social reciprocity, communication, and behavioral flexibility
Intellectual ability and language level vary widely; normal intelligence does not exclude diagnosis
Older exam term: **pervasive developmental disorder**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **M-CHAT-R/F at 18 and 24 months**; developmental surveillance at every well visit
Positive screen → follow-up interview when required, comprehensive developmental evaluation; screening alone never diagnoses
★ Confirm all 3 social domains + ≥2 repetitive/restricted domains, early onset, functional impairment
**Audiology first** for language delay, regression, or apparent deafness; assess cognition, adaptive skills, comorbidities
Offer chromosomal microarray and fragile X evaluation; EEG only for seizure concern or atypical regression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Early intervention referral immediately**, without awaiting definitive diagnostic testing
Individualized developmental/behavioral intervention, speech-language support, occupational services, school accommodations
Parent-mediated skill building and communication supports; target practical function and participation
Severe dangerous irritability → risperidone or aripiprazole; no drug treats core social deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: Anxiety, ADHD, epilepsy, sleep disturbance, feeding selectivity; wandering and self-injury risks
Antipsychotics → weight gain, metabolic abnormalities, movement disorders

rows.label: Prevention
items: Family genetic counseling, sibling developmental monitoring; no established primary preventive intervention
Safety planning for wandering, water exposure, and caregiver support

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hearing loss: impaired sound response without characteristic repetitive behaviors
Language disorder: preserved nonverbal reciprocity and shared interests
Social communication disorder: social-language deficits without restricted repetitive behaviors

autism-spectrum-disorder.evidence: Checked screening/early referral 2026-10-30: [AAP autism resources](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-behavioral-pediatrics-a-resource-guide-for-general-pediatricians/autism-spectrum-disorder-resources-for-pediatricians/); diagnostic criteria established DSM-5-TR teaching.

bell-palsy.name: Bell palsy
bell-palsy.scope: Idiopathic facial nerve (CN VII) palsy, forehead involvement vs central sparing, eye care, oral glucocorticoids, Lyme disease facial palsy
bell-palsy.core: Acute unilateral peripheral facial weakness includes the forehead; protect the cornea and treat early after excluding secondary causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pregnancy/postpartum period, diabetes; often follows viral illness
Tick exposure/endemic region suggests Lyme; otalgia with vesicles suggests varicella-zoster

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid onset over hours, maximal within 72 hours; drooping mouth and incomplete eyelid closure
Flattened nasolabial fold, impaired taste anterior tongue, hyperacusis; otherwise normal neurologic examination
★ Limb weakness, aphasia, diplopia or ataxia → **stroke/brainstem lesion evaluation**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation and edema of CN VII within facial canal impair ipsilateral facial muscles
Supranuclear lesions usually spare upper facial movement because of bilateral cortical innervation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; document forehead movement, eye closure, ear findings and other cranial nerves
Lyme serology for compatible exposure, bilateral palsy, meningitic symptoms or systemic features
MRI for progressive, recurrent same-side, atypical or persistent palsy; no routine imaging for typical presentation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oral prednisone within 72 hours**; consider added valacyclovir for severe/complete paralysis
★ **Artificial tears**, nighttime eye ointment and taping; urgent ophthalmology for corneal injury
Lyme-associated palsy → doxycycline or ceftriaxone according to neurologic involvement; steroid benefit uncertain
