Ramsay Hunt syndrome → valacyclovir plus glucocorticoid; antivirals alone insufficient for idiopathic palsy

rows.label: Complications
items: Exposure keratitis/ulceration, synkinesis, facial contracture, incomplete recovery
Aberrant reinnervation → crocodile tears during eating

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tick avoidance reduces Lyme-associated disease; no proven primary prevention for idiopathic episodes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Central hemispheric stroke: contralateral lower-face weakness, forehead usually spared
Parotid tumor: gradual progression or palpable mass; otitis: infectious ear findings

bell-palsy.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
Uncertain pigmented lesion → dermoscopy and biopsy; do not destroy before excluding melanoma
Suspicious deep mass → MRI and specialist-directed biopsy; ultrasound can establish superficial cystic character

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance** for confidently benign, untroublesome lesions; treatment chosen for symptoms or cosmetic goals
Irritated keratosis/tag → cryotherapy, snip, or shave removal; dermatofibroma usually observed
Symptomatic lipoma → excision; large/deep or suspicious masses need evaluation before office removal
★ Epidermoid cyst → **complete capsule excision** after inflammation subsides; fluctuant abscess → incision/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Local irritation, secondary infection, cyst rupture; removal → bleeding, scar, recurrence
Premature reassurance of atypical growth can delay cancer diagnosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Melanoma: evolving asymmetric pigmentation, irregular border, color variation
Squamous cell carcinoma: indurated, scaly or ulcerated enlarging lesion
Liposarcoma: deep progressive mass rather than small soft mobile nodule

table.title: Morphologic recognition
rows: Firm papule; dimples with lateral compression

benign-skin-growths.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatologic morphology and evaluation principles.

bipolar-disorder.name: Bipolar disorder
bipolar-disorder.scope: Bipolar I (manic episode, DIG FAST), bipolar II (hypomania and major depression), cyclothymic disorder, acute mania pharmacotherapy (antipsychotics, lithium, valproate), maintenance therapy
bipolar-disorder.core: Distinct episodes of pathologically increased energy with elevated or irritable mood distinguish bipolar illness from ordinary mood variability.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong family history; typical onset adolescence/young adulthood
Sleep deprivation, antidepressants, stimulants, substances can precipitate episodes

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **DIG FAST**: distractibility, impulsivity, grandiosity, flight of ideas, activity, decreased sleep need, talkativeness
≥3 associated symptoms; ≥4 if mood only irritable
Mania: psychosis, marked impairment, risky spending/sex, or hospitalization; reduced sleep without fatigue

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial genetic vulnerability with dysregulated mood, reward and circadian systems

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical longitudinal history + collateral**; ask about prior elevated episodes before treating depression
Assess suicidality, pregnancy, substance use; TSH, metabolic panel, toxicology to exclude secondary causes
Hospitalization requirement can establish manic duration criterion even before one week
Major depression ≥2 weeks; hypomania causes no psychosis, marked impairment or hospitalization
Cyclothymia: symptoms ≥half the time; no symptom-free interval >2 months or full mood episodes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mania → **antipsychotic** (olanzapine/quetiapine); severe → add lithium/valproate; mixed/rapid cycling → **divalproex**
Unsafe, psychotic, severely agitated, or unable to care for self → hospitalization
Depression → quetiapine, lurasidone, lithium, lamotrigine; urgent/refractory or first-trimester psychotic mania → **ECT**
★ **Avoid antidepressant monotherapy**; lamotrigine does not treat acute mania
Maintenance: lithium, quetiapine, valproate or lamotrigine selected by episode pattern; lithium reduces suicide risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, substance misuse, financial/relationship loss; metabolic adverse effects of antipsychotics
Lithium: renal/thyroid toxicity; valproate/carbamazepine: teratogenicity, avoid in first trimester; lamotrigine: severe rash

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular sleep, psychoeducation, relapse-sign monitoring, maintenance adherence; avoid stimulants and substance misuse

rows.label: Mimics
items: ADHD: chronic baseline symptoms rather than distinct mood episodes
Borderline personality: brief reactive shifts linked to interpersonal stress
Medication/substance-induced mania: onset after antidepressant, stimulant, steroid → **stop culprit first**
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, tremor, low TSH

table.title: Diagnostic branches
rows: Hypomania ≥4 days + major depression; never mania

bladder-cancer.name: Bladder cancer
bladder-cancer.scope: Urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, painless gross hematuria, smoking and occupational exposures, cystoscopy, transurethral resection
bladder-cancer.core: Painless gross hematuria in an older adult requires evaluation for urinary tract malignancy, even during anticoagulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Smoking**, aromatic amines in dye/rubber industries; older age and male sex
Cyclophosphamide, pelvic radiation; chronic catheter irritation and Schistosoma haematobium predispose to squamous carcinoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Intermittent bleeding, clots; carcinoma in situ may produce irritative voiding symptoms without a visible mass
Advanced disease: pelvic pain, hydronephrosis, weight loss, or bone pain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urothelial field injury → multifocal tumors and recurrence throughout the collecting system
Squamous metaplasia from chronic inflammation → keratinizing malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Cystoscopy + CT urography** evaluate bladder and upper tracts; urinalysis/culture assess alternatives
Urine cytology helps detect high-grade disease/CIS; negative cytology does not exclude cancer
★ **TURBT including muscularis propria** establishes histology, grade, and depth
T1 disease → repeat resection within 6 weeks; invasive disease → chest/abdomen/pelvis staging

rows.label: Tx
items: Clot retention → large-bore catheter, irrigation; persistent obstruction or bleeding → urgent urology
Selected fit patients seeking bladder preservation → maximal resection plus concurrent chemoradiation
Avoid intravesical chemotherapy with suspected bladder perforation; BCG contraindicated during active symptomatic UTI

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive renal failure, recurrent hemorrhage, nodal or distant metastases
Intravesical BCG → cystitis; rarely disseminated infection; cystectomy → diversion-related metabolic complications

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and occupational protection; no routine population screening
★ **Surveillance cystoscopy** after treatment because recurrence is common; interval based on risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nephrolithiasis: colicky flank pain, stone on noncontrast CT
Glomerulonephritis: dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, proteinuria
Cystitis: dysuria and positive culture; persistent hematuria after treatment still needs evaluation
Urethral carcinoma: older woman, blood spotting, friable urethral meatal mass, irritative/obstructive voiding

table.title: Depth determines definitive treatment
rows: TURBT + intravesical BCG; selected early cystectomy

bone-tumors.name: Bone tumors
bone-tumors.scope: Osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor of bone, osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, bone metastases, biopsy
bone-tumors.core: Persistent focal bone pain, a growing mass, or a destructive radiographic lesion requires planned evaluation before biopsy or fixation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteosarcoma: adolescence, hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1), prior radiation, Paget disease; chondrosarcoma: older adults
Hereditary multiple exostoses predispose to osteochondromas; most adult malignant bone lesions are metastases

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Night/rest pain**, enlarging mass, constitutional symptoms or pathologic fracture → concerning lesion
Osteoid osteoma: nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs; small cortical nidus
Osteochondroma: painless metaphyseal exostosis with medullary continuity; new growth after maturity concerning
Known cancer + constant back pain, vertebral point tenderness → **spinal metastasis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor lineage determines osteoid, cartilage or primitive-cell production; aggressive growth destroys cortex
Giant cell tumor: neoplastic stromal cells recruit osteoclast-like giant cells, causing locally aggressive osteolysis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs first**; assess location, margins, periosteal reaction and matrix
Aggressive lesion → MRI entire involved bone/adjacent joint; chest CT for lung metastases
★ **Orthopedic oncology plans biopsy tract**; core biopsy after imaging, before definitive treatment
CBC, ESR/CRP if infection suspected; normal labs do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Osteosarcoma → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection**, then postoperative chemotherapy
Ewing → systemic chemotherapy plus surgery and/or radiation
Chondrosarcoma → wide surgical excision; conventional tumors relatively chemo/radioresistant
Symptomatic osteoid osteoma → radiofrequency ablation; asymptomatic osteochondroma → observation
Giant cell tumor → curettage/reconstruction; selected unresectable lesions → denosumab

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fracture, neurovascular compromise, pulmonary metastases; limb surgery and chemotherapy morbidity
Mandible metastasis → mental nerve anesthesia (**numb chin**)

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: infection markers, cultures; may closely resemble Ewing
Bone metastases: older adult, multiple lesions; myeloma: anemia, monoclonal protein
Unicameral bone cyst: child, lucent expansile proximal humerus lesion; pathologic fracture after minor trauma

bone-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery (**adhesions**, leading cause), incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Complete → **obstipation**, no flatus; partial may still pass stool/diarrhea, not excluding obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels, no rectal gas; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain
★ Massive colonic distention + **coffee-bean (inverted-U) loop** on radiograph → sigmoid volvulus
Pregnancy: plain radiograph acceptable first (minimal fetal dose); MRI if unclear; do not delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs
Ileus: hypoactive/absent sounds, gas throughout bowel including rectum
Diabetic autonomic neuropathy: dysmotility, dilated loops without transition point

table.title: Large-bowel branches
rows: Sigmoidoscopic detorsion, rectal tube → same-admission resection

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance
Child: chronic cough refractory to bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics + persistent focal collapse/consolidation → localized bronchiectasis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura, cystic spaces ± air-fluid levels
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: solitary cavity with air-fluid level; no lifelong productive cough
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

caustic-ingestion.name: Caustic ingestion
caustic-ingestion.scope: Acid and alkali ingestion, airway assessment, contraindications to emesis or neutralization, early esophagogastroduodenoscopy within 24 hours, stricture complications
caustic-ingestion.core: Corrosive ingestion can burn the airway and gastrointestinal tract; a normal mouth examination does not exclude deep injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young children: accidental household cleaner exposure; adults: intentional large-volume ingestion
Drain/oven cleaners (NaOH), industrial acids; bleach usually mild; concentration, contact time determine severity

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral burns/ulcers, drooling, odynophagia, dysphagia, vomiting, hematemesis, chest or abdominal pain
★ **Stridor, hoarseness, respiratory distress** → threatened airway
Severe tenderness, rigidity, fever, shock → transmural necrosis or perforation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alkali: liquefactive necrosis, deep esophageal penetration; acid: coagulative necrosis, often gastric injury
Both agents can injure the entire upper gastrointestinal tract; eschar provides incomplete protection

rows.label: Dx
items: Identify substance, concentration, amount, time; poison control consultation
★ Stable symptomatic/significant exposure → **EGD within 24 hours** for injury grading
Suspected perforation/necrosis → contrast CT chest/abdomen and surgery consultation; avoid diagnostic endoscopy if perforated
CBC, electrolytes, renal function, lactate, blood gas; normal labs cannot exclude injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Airway first**; early controlled intubation with direct visualization when swelling progresses
NPO, IV crystalloid, analgesia; surgical treatment for perforation or full-thickness necrosis
★ **No emesis, neutralization, gastric lavage, or activated charcoal**; additional burns or heat generation
Avoid blind NG placement; no routine corticosteroids or prophylactic antibiotics

rows.label: Complications
items: Mediastinitis, peritonitis, hemorrhage, fistula; delayed esophageal stricture or gastric outlet obstruction
Long-term esophageal squamous cell carcinoma risk; strictures may require repeated dilation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Locked storage in original labeled containers; never transfer chemicals into beverage bottles
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment after stabilization; swallowing/nutrition follow-up after severe injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Esophageal foreign body: discrete obstruction on history or imaging
Pill esophagitis: medication exposure, focal ulceration without extensive chemical burns

caustic-ingestion.evidence: Not checked online; established toxicology teaching.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

chronic-venous-insufficiency.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
chronic-venous-insufficiency.scope: Varicose veins, stasis dermatitis, venous stasis ulcers, superficial thrombophlebitis, post-thrombotic syndrome
chronic-venous-insufficiency.core: Venous hypertension produces dependent edema, hemosiderin pigmentation, and shallow medial ankle ulcers that improve with elevation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior DVT, obesity, pregnancy, prolonged standing, older age, family history
Reduced calf-muscle pumping from immobility; previous leg trauma or venous surgery

rows.label: Clues
items: Aching/heaviness worsened by standing; varicosities, pitting swelling, preserved pedal pulses
Eczematous itching, lipodermatosclerosis, inverted champagne-bottle leg contour
★ **Irregular, exudative gaiter-region wound**; bilateral erythema without systemic illness favors stasis dermatitis
Superficial thrombophlebitis: focal erythema over a tender palpable venous cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Valve failure or outflow obstruction → reflux, capillary leakage, chronic inflammation
Post-thrombotic syndrome: residual obstruction and valvular injury following DVT

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Venous duplex ultrasound** evaluates reflux and obstruction; clinical examination often establishes diagnosis
★ **Ankle-brachial index before compression** when PAD suspected; <0.5 → avoid sustained compression
Nonhealing or atypical ulcer → biopsy for malignancy; sudden unilateral worsening → evaluate acute DVT
New superficial cord → assess clot length, proximity to deep junction, associated DVT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adequate arterial inflow → **compression bandaging/stockings + leg elevation**; walking activates calf pump
Ulcers: saline cleansing, moist absorbent dressings, debridement when needed
Stasis dermatitis: emollients + short-course topical steroid on intact skin; weeping → saline-soaked dressings, elevation
Symptomatic superficial reflux → endovenous ablation; moderate arterial disease → specialist-guided reduced compression
No antibiotics for colonization alone; cellulitis → systemic antibiotics; no routine diuretics without volume overload

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent ulceration, cellulitis, contact dermatitis; superficial clot can extend into deep veins
Chronic wounds rarely undergo squamous malignant transformation; new growth or bleeding warrants biopsy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight reduction, regular mobility, avoid prolonged dependent posture
Long-term compression after ulcer healing reduces recurrence; moisturize skin and treat venous reflux

rows.label: Mimics
items: Arterial ulcer: painful punched-out toes/lateral ankle, cool foot, weak pulses
Neuropathic ulcer: plantar pressure points, sensory loss, callus
Lymphedema: dorsal foot/toe swelling, later nonpitting thickened skin

table.title: Superficial thrombosis treatment
rows: Short distal segment, no high-risk features
≥5 cm long, >3 cm from deep junction

chronic-venous-insufficiency.evidence: Thrombosis checked 2026-10-30: [SVS/AVF/AVLS 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11523430/); wound care established teaching.

cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.name: Cirrhosis and portal hypertension
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.scope: Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, esophageal varices, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma screening
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.core: Cirrhosis produces portal hypertension and synthetic failure; new ascites, bleeding, confusion or kidney injury signals decompensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol, chronic HBV/HCV, metabolic steatotic liver disease; autoimmune/cholestatic disorders

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, spider angiomas, jaundice, muscle wasting
Encephalopathy: **asterixis**; triggers GI bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives, hypokalemia, protein load
SBP may present only with subtle confusion or renal deterioration; fever/pain can be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fibrosis raises intrahepatic resistance; splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume
Portal collaterals bleed; impaired toxin clearance causes neuropsychiatric dysfunction
SBP: **intestinal bacterial translocation** into ascitic fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New/worsening or hospitalized ascites → **diagnostic paracentesis**; PMN **≥250/µL** → treat SBP
SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension; send ascitic culture in bedside blood-culture bottles
HRS-AKI: exclude shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and structural injury; assess volume response
MELD-Na/MELD 3.0 guides prognosis/transplant assessment
Encephalopathy clinical: **ammonia** not diagnostic; older exam questions may expect serum ammonia after normal head CT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Variceal bleed → resuscitate, **octreotide + ceftriaxone**, urgent endoscopic banding; refractory → TIPS
Ascites → sodium restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide; tense ascites → paracentesis, albumin if >5 L
★ SBP → **ceftriaxone**, albumin for high-risk renal/liver dysfunction; reassess response
Encephalopathy → lactulose to 2–3 soft stools/day, rifaximin (add for recurrence); correct trigger; no sedatives
HRS → stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, **terlipressin + albumin** after volume assessment; monitor hypoxia; transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HCC, recurrent infection, malnutrition, hepatopulmonary syndrome; TIPS can worsen encephalopathy
Avoid NSAIDs, sedatives and unnecessary fluid loading; INR alone poorly predicts procedural bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Ultrasound + AFP every 6 months** for HCC surveillance in eligible cirrhosis
Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension when tolerated; banding if indicated and beta blocker unsuitable
After SBP → antibiotic prophylaxis; alcohol abstinence, hepatitis vaccines, adequate protein intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiac ascites: high SAAG with ascitic protein ≥2.5 g/dL
Malignant/TB ascites: usually low SAAG

cleft-lip-and-palate.name: Cleft lip and palate
cleft-lip-and-palate.scope: Embryology, feeding difficulties, Eustachian tube dysfunction and otitis media, velopharyngeal insufficiency, speech resonance disorders, surgical timing
cleft-lip-and-palate.core: Visible lip or palatal defect at birth, with poor suction or nasal regurgitation when the palate is involved.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, maternal smoking, pregestational diabetes, teratogens such as valproate

rows.label: Clues
items: Isolated cleft lip may permit effective breastfeeding; cleft palate often requires assisted feeding
Submucous cleft: bifid uvula, translucent midline, posterior hard palate notch

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ Lip: failed fusion of maxillary and medial nasal prominences
★ Palate: failed fusion of lateral palatal shelves
Abnormal palatal musculature impairs Eustachian tube opening and nasopharyngeal closure

rows.label: Dx
items: Inspect and palpate entire palate; assess growth, associated anomalies and syndromic features
Newborn hearing screen plus serial audiology and middle ear assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Upright feeds with specialty squeezable bottle; monitor weight and intake
★ Multidisciplinary repair: lip typically 2–6 months; palate commonly 9–18 months, before established speech
Persistent effusion or hearing loss → assess for tympanostomy tubes
Speech therapy for learned articulation errors; persistent structural insufficiency → surgical assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent otitis media with effusion, conductive hearing loss, dental malalignment
Velopharyngeal insufficiency → hypernasality and audible nasal air escape

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preconception folic acid, smoking cessation, diabetes control, medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ankyloglossia: restricted tongue excursion with intact palate
Choanal atresia: cyanosis during feeds relieved by crying

cleft-lip-and-palate.evidence: Checked cleft repair timing against American Society of Plastic Surgeons guidance.

colorectal-cancer-screening.name: Colorectal cancer screening
colorectal-cancer-screening.scope: Average-risk screening age 45-75, colonoscopy, FIT, high-risk screening (family history, Lynch syndrome, IBD), post-polypectomy surveillance
colorectal-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk adults ages 45–75; every positive noncolonoscopy screening test requires diagnostic colonoscopy.

rows.label: Who
items: Average risk: no CRC/adenoma history, IBD or hereditary syndrome; FDR = first-degree relative
★ Symptoms or iron deficiency anemia → **diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening age
FDR CRC/advanced polyp <60 or ≥2 affected FDRs → high-risk family pathway

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Ages 76–85: individualize by health, preference and prior screening; stop after 85
★ High-risk family → start **40 or 10 years before youngest diagnosis**, whichever earlier
Family-risk colonoscopy every 5 years; one FDR ≥60 → start 40, routine intervals

rows.label: Test
items: ★ **Colonoscopy every 10 years** or **FIT annually** are common strategies
Stool DNA–FIT every 1–3 years; CT colonography every 5 years
Flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, or every 10 years plus annual FIT

rows.label: IF positive
items: Positive FIT/stool DNA/CT study → colonoscopy; repeating stool test cannot clear the result
Post-polypectomy intervals assume complete removal, adequate preparation and high-quality examination

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Lynch: colonoscopy roughly age 20–25 every 1–2 years; gene/family history can modify
Colonic IBD: surveillance about 8 years after onset; PSC → begin at diagnosis
Routine stool testing between scheduled high-quality surveillance colonoscopies adds little benefit

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

congenital-urinary-tract-anomalies.name: Congenital urinary tract anomalies
congenital-urinary-tract-anomalies.scope: Posterior urethral valves (oligohydramnios, palpable bladder, VCUG, ablation), vesicoureteral reflux (hydronephrosis, recurrent UTI), ureteropelvic junction obstruction, cryptorchidism, hypospadias
congenital-urinary-tract-anomalies.core: Prenatal collecting-system dilation, recurrent febrile UTI, or abnormal genital examination requires localization of obstruction, reflux, or disordered development.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Posterior urethral valves occur only in boys; reflux may cluster in families
Cryptorchidism: prematurity, low birth weight; hypospadias: disrupted urethral development

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Boy with **weak stream, palpable bladder**, bilateral hydronephrosis → outlet obstruction
Severe fetal obstruction → oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, Potter sequence
Recurrent febrile UTIs, poor growth, hypertension may signal reflux nephropathy
★ Hypospadias + bilateral nonpalpable testes → urgent disorder-of-sex-development evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: High urinary pressure or retrograde infected urine damages developing renal parenchyma
Undescended testes experience thermal injury; ectopic ventral meatus may accompany chordee

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Renal/bladder **ultrasound** first; creatinine, electrolytes, urinalysis/culture assess consequences
VCUG after abnormal ultrasound suggesting reflux/obstruction or recurrent febrile UTIs; not every first uncomplicated UTI
UPJ dilation without hydroureter → MAG3 diuretic renography for drainage and differential function
Cryptorchidism: examination; no pre-referral ultrasound; bilateral nonpalpable testes → endocrine/genetic evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Valves: bladder catheter decompression, correct fluids/electrolytes → endoscopic **valve ablation**
Reflux: low-risk → observation; high-risk → consider TMP-SMX prophylaxis; breakthrough febrile UTIs → ureteral reimplantation
UPJ obstruction: observe preserved function; worsening drainage/function or symptoms → pyeloplasty
Cryptorchidism: refer at 6 months corrected age; orchiopexy by 18 months
★ Hypospadias: **defer circumcision**; foreskin may support reconstruction; repair generally 6–18 months

rows.label: Complications
items: Renal scarring, CKD, hypertension; valve bladder dysfunction may persist after successful ablation
Cryptorchidism: subfertility, torsion, malignancy; orchiopexy reduces but does not eliminate cancer risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat constipation and dysfunctional voiding to reduce recurrent UTIs
Prompt fever evaluation and long-term BP/renal-function surveillance after significant reflux or obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Retractile testis: can remain in scrotum after manipulation; monitor annually for ascent
Physiologic neonatal dilation: resolves without progressive functional loss

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

cystic-fibrosis.name: Cystic fibrosis
cystic-fibrosis.scope: CFTR mutations, meconium ileus, bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, sweat chloride test
cystic-fibrosis.core: Recurrent sinopulmonary infection plus malabsorption, poor growth or neonatal meconium ileus suggests CFTR dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive CFTR variants; affected sibling or carrier parents
F508del is common; genotype determines eligibility for specific CFTR modulators

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic productive cough, recurrent pneumonia, nasal polyps, clubbing and bronchiectasis
Greasy stools, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive despite appetite
Salty skin, dehydration with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; male infertility from absent vas deferens
Neonatal abdominal distention with inspissated ileal meconium; later rectal prolapse possible

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective apical chloride/bicarbonate transport → dehydrated airway and pancreatic secretions
Sweat ducts fail to reabsorb chloride; pancreatic duct blockage causes exocrine destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive newborn immunoreactive trypsinogen screen → **quantitative sweat chloride** confirmation
★ Sweat chloride **≥60 mmol/L** supports CF; 30–59 intermediate → repeat/genetic evaluation
Two CF-causing variants in trans or specialized CFTR-function testing resolve uncertain cases
Fecal elastase assesses pancreatic insufficiency; sputum cultures guide respiratory antibiotics
Consider CF despite negative limited mutation panel when clinical phenotype is compelling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, hypertonic saline, dornase alfa; exercise supports mucus clearance
Pulmonary exacerbation → culture-directed antibiotics; Pseudomonas commonly needs antipseudomonal coverage
★ Pancreatic insufficiency → **pancrelipase with meals**, high-calorie nutrition, vitamins A/D/E/K
Eligible genotype → elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor; check liver function and interactions
Advanced respiratory failure → oxygen/ventilatory support and lung transplant assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas colonization, massive hemoptysis, pneumothorax, respiratory failure
CF-related diabetes, biliary liver disease, distal intestinal obstruction, osteoporosis and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccination, nutrition monitoring, salt/fluid replacement during heat or exercise
Infection-control separation between CF patients; family carrier testing and reproductive counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary ciliary dyskinesia: situs inversus possible; normal pancreatic function/sweat chloride
Immunodeficiency: recurrent infection without CFTR-pattern salt loss
Celiac disease: malabsorption without bronchiectasis

cystic-fibrosis.evidence: Diagnostic threshold checked 2026-10-30: [CF Foundation sweat testing](https://www.cff.org/intro-cf/sweat-test); management established CF teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age: strongest Alzheimer risk; early-onset first-degree family history; Down syndrome (APP triplication)
Vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Alzheimer: hippocampal loss → poor delayed/episodic recall; **nucleus basalis of Meynert** loss → acetylcholine deficit
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval, preserved independence → reassurance; MCI: objective deficit, independence preserved
Typical Alzheimer: clinical diagnosis after routine labs/imaging; **APOE genotyping not indicated**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy/Parkinson disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA
Parkinson dementia psychosis/agitation → **quetiapine** over haloperidol; clozapine needs agranulocytosis monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage
Parkinson disease: dementia strongest predictor of nursing home placement and mortality

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Visuospatial deficit, e.g., failed pentagon copy → **no car keys** until formal driving assessment
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

dermatophyte-infections.name: Dermatophyte infections
dermatophyte-infections.scope: Tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, onychomycosis, potassium hydroxide preparation, oral and topical antifungals
dermatophyte-infections.core: Keratin-invading fungi cause scaly skin lesions or infected hair/nails; the anatomic site determines topical versus systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Warm humid conditions, occlusive footwear, shared showers, wrestling, infected animals or contacts
Diabetes, immunosuppression; childhood favors scalp infection; nail disease increases with age

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus and peripheral scaling; steroid exposure may distort borders and suppress inflammation
★ **Boggy tender scalp plaque** → kerion; inflammatory disease risks permanent scarring alopecia
Interdigital maceration/fissures can become bacterial entry sites

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton digest keratin in stratum corneum, hair, and nails
**T rubrum** most common on skin/nails; capitis → **T tonsurans** (endothrix)
Follicular/deep involvement prevents topical agents from reaching the infected reservoir

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **KOH preparation of active edge** → branching septate hyphae; obtain before systemic treatment when uncertain
Scalp: hair/plucked scale microscopy and culture; nail: clipping KOH, PAS, or fungal culture
Wood lamp detects only selected organisms; negative fluorescence does not exclude tinea
Refractory/widespread infection → reassess diagnosis, adherence, resistance; fungal culture can guide further care

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Limited skin disease → **topical terbinafine** or clotrimazole; continue beyond clinical clearing
★ Hair infection → **oral griseofulvin or terbinafine**; adjunct selenium sulfide/ketoconazole shampoo reduces spread
Nail infection → confirm fungus, then oral terbinafine; baseline liver assessment; counsel slow regrowth
Avoid topical corticosteroid monotherapy or steroid-antifungal combinations; extensive disease may require oral antifungal

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary cellulitis, persistent nail dystrophy, recurrent infection from untreated reservoirs
Oral antifungals: hepatotoxicity, drug interactions; griseofulvin contraindicated during pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Keep feet dry**, change socks, avoid shared towels/combs, disinfect sports gear
Treat symptomatic contacts/pets and coexisting tinea pedis (autoinfects groin → recurrence); avoid barefoot communal-shower exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candida intertrigo: satellite pustules, scrotal involvement
Psoriasis: sharply demarcated plaques, nail pitting; alopecia areata: smooth nonscaly patches

table.title: Site clues
rows: Broken hairs, black dots, patchy alopecia, occipital nodes
Annular plaque, advancing border, central clearing
Thick yellow brittle nail, subungual debris

dermatophyte-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatophyte diagnosis and site-based treatment.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.scope: Acute vs chronic DIC, sepsis, malignancy, obstetric complications, coagulopathy (prolonged PT/PTT, low fibrinogen, elevated D-dimer, schistocytes), blood product replacement
disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.core: Systemic coagulation activation simultaneously causes microvascular thrombosis and consumption of platelets/clotting factors, producing organ injury and bleeding.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sepsis, severe trauma/burns, shock, acute pancreatitis
Obstetric emergencies: abruption, amniotic fluid embolism, retained fetal demise
Malignancy: especially acute promyelocytic leukemia, advanced adenocarcinoma; large vascular abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Oozing from IV sites**, mucosal bleeding, widespread ecchymoses in a severely ill patient
Digital ischemia, purpura fulminans, altered mental status, oliguria suggest microthrombi
Chronic compensated disease may present predominantly with venous/arterial thrombosis rather than hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue-factor-driven thrombin generation → fibrin deposition; secondary fibrinolysis increases degradation products
Rapid consumption overwhelms hepatic/marrow replacement in acute disease; slower activation allows partial compensation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **↓Platelets, ↑PT/PTT, ↑D-dimer, ↓fibrinogen**; schistocytes may accompany microangiopathic hemolysis
Serial values and clinical trigger matter; early sepsis can preserve fibrinogen as an acute-phase reactant
CBC/smear, coagulation panel, fibrinogen, renal/liver function; cultures or obstetric evaluation identify cause
ISTH score uses platelets, PT, fibrin marker, fibrinogen; repeat when evolving
Fibrinogen drives rouleaux/ESR; consumption → **paradoxically falling ESR**, not recovery

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat underlying cause** immediately: antibiotics/source control, obstetric delivery, leukemia-directed treatment
Bleeding or invasive procedure with platelets <50,000/µL → platelet transfusion
★ Bleeding with factor depletion → **FFP**; fibrinogen <100–150 mg/dL → cryoprecipitate
Thrombosis-predominant chronic disease → selected heparin use; avoid during uncontrolled hemorrhage
No blood products solely to normalize labs in nonbleeding stable disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Multiorgan failure, diffuse hemorrhage, limb ischemia/gangrene, death
Transfusion complications: volume overload, lung injury; anticoagulation can worsen bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Prompt sepsis treatment, hemorrhage control, obstetric complication management; monitor high-risk triggers closely

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP/HUS: thrombocytopenia and hemolysis with usually normal PT/PTT
Liver failure: impaired synthesis with hepatic disease; clinical context and trends distinguish
HIT: heparin-linked platelet fall, thrombosis, usually preserved coagulation tests

disseminated-intravascular-coagulation.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology teaching.

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient: amoxicillin-clavulanate (older exams: ciprofloxacin/metronidazole); severe: ceftriaxone/metronidazole or pip-tazo
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.name: Dyspepsia and peptic ulcer disease
dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.scope: Uninvestigated dyspepsia (age < 60 test-and-treat vs age >= 60 endoscopy), Helicobacter pylori testing and eradication, gastric and duodenal ulcers
dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.core: Epigastric discomfort may reflect functional dyspepsia or acid-peptic ulceration; age and bleeding risk determine noninvasive testing versus endoscopy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: H pylori, NSAIDs/aspirin; smoking impairs healing
Prior ulcer bleeding, anticoagulants, older age amplify NSAID harm; severe physiologic stress causes ICU ulcers

rows.label: Clues
items: Epigastric burning, early satiety, nausea; meal timing cannot reliably distinguish ulcer location
★ **Alarm**: hematemesis/melena, positive occult blood, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, weight loss, iron-deficiency anemia
Sudden rigid abdomen → perforation
Early satiety, nonbilious vomiting, succussion splash, gastric distention → gastric outlet obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: H pylori or prostaglandin depletion weakens mucosal defenses against acid-pepsin injury
Antral-predominant infection increases acid; corpus-predominant inflammation may cause atrophy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New dyspepsia **≥60 years or any alarm feature → upper endoscopy**
★ Under 60 without concerning features → **urea breath or stool antigen test**
Hold PPI 2 weeks and antibiotics/bismuth 4 weeks before active-infection testing; serology cannot confirm eradication
Gastric ulcer → biopsy to exclude malignancy; duodenal ulcers rarely malignant
Refractory/recurrent multiple ulcers + diarrhea → fasting gastrin with careful PPI interpretation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ H pylori → **14-day bismuth quadruple**: PPI + bismuth + tetracycline + metronidazole
Avoid empiric clarithromycin/levofloxacin regimens unless susceptibility demonstrated
Negative infection test or persistent symptoms after eradication → PPI trial; functional symptoms may need TCA
