rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected mold pneumonia → **chest CT**, bronchoscopy/BAL or tissue biopsy
Aspergillus galactomannan in serum/BAL; β-D-glucan supports several fungi but usually negative in mucormycosis
Necrotic sinus lesion → urgent endoscopic biopsy for histology/culture; do not await blood cultures
Candidemia → repeat blood cultures until clear; assess source and metastatic foci
ABPA: Aspergillus-IgE + total IgE ≥500 IU/mL; two of eosinophilia, Aspergillus-IgG, CT bronchiectasis/infiltrates

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aspergillosis → **voriconazole** or isavuconazole; evaluate interactions and liver function
★ Mucormycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B + urgent surgical debridement**; correct DKA/immunosuppression
Candidemia → echinocandin such as micafungin; step down to fluconazole when stable, susceptible and cleared
Remove implicated line when feasible; uncomplicated candidemia → ≥14 days after clearance and symptom resolution
ABPA → prednisolone or itraconazole; recurrent flares → both; avoid steroids for untreated invasive disease

rows.label: Complications
items: CNS dissemination, massive hemoptysis, blindness, endocarditis; high mortality if treatment delayed
Amphotericin → AKI, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia; voriconazole → visual effects, hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Selected high-risk prolonged neutropenia → posaconazole prophylaxis; line hygiene and antibiotic stewardship

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum: necrotic skin lesions with bacterial sepsis
Bacterial abscess: pyogenic cultures; malignancy: tissue without invasive organisms

low-back-pain.name: Low back pain
low-back-pain.scope: Lumbosacral strain, herniated disk and radiculopathy, spinal stenosis, red flags, imaging indications, conservative management
low-back-pain.core: Most acute low back pain improves with activity and analgesia; neurologic deficits or systemic red flags change the workup.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heavy lifting, deconditioning, obesity, prolonged sitting
Cancer, immunosuppression, injection drug use, osteoporosis, chronic glucocorticoids increase serious-pathology risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Mechanical pain varies with movement; isolated axial pain without systemic illness favors benign disease
★ **Urinary retention, saddle anesthesia, bilateral weakness** → cauda equina emergency
Fever, weight loss, night pain, trauma, or progressive weakness → targeted urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Paraspinal injury causes localized pain; degenerative narrowing or disk extrusion compresses neural structures

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No red flags → **no initial imaging**, including routine radiographs
Focused strength, reflex, sensory, gait examination; straight-leg raise supports lower lumbar radiculopathy
★ Suspected infection, malignancy, cord compression → **MRI**; suspected fracture → radiograph or CT
Persistent symptoms despite about 6 weeks' care → MRI if intervention being considered
Suspected spinal infection → ESR/CRP, blood cultures; normal temperature does not exclude infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Continue activity**, no heavy lifting until pain resolves, heat, short NSAID course; avoid prolonged bed rest
Physical therapy if pain persists despite NSAIDs; avoid routine opioids and systemic steroids
Progressive motor deficit or cauda equina → urgent surgical decompression
Refractory disabling radicular pain → epidural injection or diskectomy after imaging correlation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic pain, functional limitation, medication dependence
Untreated compression → permanent bladder, bowel, sexual, or motor dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Core strengthening, regular exercise, ergonomic lifting, weight management

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: abdominal pulsatile mass, vascular risk, hypotension
Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; inflammatory back pain: improves with exercise
Vascular claudication: calf pain, bicycling too; standing still relieves; weak pulses alone don't exclude stenosis

table.title: Mechanical patterns
rows: Leg pain below knee; cough aggravates
Shopping-cart sign; pulses usually preserved; MRI confirms

low-back-pain.evidence: Not checked online; established generalist back-pain evaluation.

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers
Leading cause of cancer death in men and women; smoking is the predominant risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action
Painful long-bone periostitis ± clubbing/joint swelling → **hypertrophic osteoarthropathy**, a lung cancer complication

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes
Central endobronchial tumor → bronchial obstruction → **post-obstructive pneumonia**, atelectasis, lobar collapse
Ectopic **ACTH** (polypeptide; cortisol excess secondary) → hyperpigmentation, hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, proximal weakness

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used
SVC syndrome from small-cell → urgent **chemotherapy** ± radiation; stent if severe; diuretics not definitive

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

macular-degeneration.name: Macular degeneration
macular-degeneration.scope: Dry age-related macular degeneration (drusen), wet age-related macular degeneration (neovascularization), metamorphopsia, Amsler grid, anti-VEGF
macular-degeneration.core: Older adult with painless central visual loss, preserved peripheral vision, and straight lines appearing wavy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, cigarette smoking, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Reading and face recognition difficulty; central scotoma in advanced disease
★ Rapid decline over days to weeks → urgent assessment for wet conversion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dry: degeneration of retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors
Wet: VEGF-mediated choroidal neovascularization beneath the macula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Dilated macular exam** and OCT; fluorescein angiography if neovascular diagnosis uncertain
★ Home **Amsler grid**: cover one eye at a time; fixate center with reading correction

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Wet: serial intravitreal **anti-VEGF** such as aflibercept or ranibizumab, guided by OCT
Selected geographic atrophy → intravitreal pegcetacoplan or avacincaptad pegol to slow expansion
Low-vision rehabilitation and magnification for persistent reading or daily activity impairment

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent central vision loss from geographic atrophy or disciform scar
Pain and rapidly worsening acuity after intravitreal injection → suspect endophthalmitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **AREDS2** for intermediate AMD or advanced AMD in one eye; no benefit in early AMD
Stop smoking; avoid beta-carotene formulations in current or former smokers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cataract: diffuse blur, glare and lens opacity
Retinal detachment: flashes, floaters, peripheral curtain

macular-degeneration.evidence: Checked AAO Age-Related Macular Degeneration Preferred Practice Pattern (2026 update).

magnesium-disorders.name: Magnesium disorders
magnesium-disorders.scope: Hypomagnesemia (alcohol, PPIs, diuretics), refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia, tremors and arrhythmias, hypermagnesemia (loss of DTRs, respiratory depression), IV magnesium, calcium gluconate
magnesium-disorders.core: Consider magnesium disturbances in unexplained neuromuscular symptoms, arrhythmia, or electrolyte abnormalities resistant to replacement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low: alcohol use, diarrhea, PPIs, loop or thiazide diuretics, cisplatin
High: renal failure plus magnesium laxatives or antacids; IV magnesium for preeclampsia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Declining urine output during obstetric magnesium infusion → increased toxicity risk

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ Low Mg → renal K wasting and impaired PTH secretion/action → refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia
Excess Mg antagonizes calcium-dependent acetylcholine release and cardiac conduction

rows.label: Dx
items: Serum Mg, K, Ca, creatinine and ECG; prolonged QT or torsades with deficiency
Unclear deficiency source → urinary magnesium distinguishes renal wasting from GI loss

rows.label: Tx
items: Oral magnesium for mild asymptomatic deficiency; address offending drugs and concurrent electrolyte deficits
★ Severe or symptomatic deficiency or torsades → **IV magnesium sulfate**
★ Symptomatic excess → stop magnesium, support ventilation and give **IV calcium gluconate**
Remove excess with saline and loop diuresis if renal function adequate; dialysis for severe renal failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Deficiency: ventricular fibrillation; toxicity: heart block or cardiac arrest

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid magnesium laxatives in advanced CKD
During obstetric magnesium infusion, serial reflex, respiratory and renal monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Isolated hypocalcemia: tetany with normal Mg and response to calcium
Opioid toxicity: hypoventilation with miosis and naloxone response

magnesium-disorders.evidence: Established electrolyte management; current guidance not checked online.

measures-of-association.name: Measures of association
measures-of-association.scope: Relative risk (RR), odds ratio (OR), attributable risk (AR), absolute risk reduction (ARR), number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), hazard ratio
measures-of-association.core: Relative measures describe proportional associations; absolute measures incorporate baseline risk and determine treatment benefit or harm.

rows.label: Definition
items: CER = control event rate; EER = experimental event rate
Two-by-two table: exposed events/non-events a/b; unexposed events/non-events c/d
Relative risk reduction (RRR; vaccine efficacy) = (CER − EER)/CER = 1 − RR

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Ratio null = **1**; risk-difference null = **0**
★ Hazard ratio compares instantaneous event rates over time; not cumulative risk ratio
NNT/NNH require specified outcome and follow-up duration; always round up

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ RR: cohort/RCT; OR: case-control and logistic regression
Attributable risk: excess incidence among exposed attributable to exposure, assuming causality
HR: survival analysis with censoring; constant interpretation assumes proportional hazards

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Use proportions, not percentage numbers, in reciprocal calculations
OR approximates RR only with rare outcomes; common outcomes exaggerate relative association
Association alone cannot establish causality; confounding can distort every measure

measures-of-association.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

measures-of-disease-frequency.name: Measures of disease frequency
measures-of-disease-frequency.scope: Incidence, prevalence, cumulative incidence, incidence rate, attack rate, case fatality rate, mortality rate
measures-of-disease-frequency.core: Disease frequency requires a numerator, eligible denominator, and time frame; new events, existing disease, and deaths answer different questions.

rows.label: Definition
items: Population at risk excludes people already affected or unable to develop the outcome
Person-time sums observation until disease, death, loss to follow-up, or study end

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Prevalence ≈ incidence × average duration** in steady state; compatible time units
Longer survival increases existing disease burden even without more new diagnoses
Cumulative incidence is probability; incidence density has inverse-time units

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Variable follow-up/open cohort → **person-time denominator**; fixed cohort/interval → risk
Prevalence → service planning; attack rate → outbreak food/exposure investigation
Primary prevention → fewer new cases → monitor **incidence**, not prevalence

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case fatality denominator: cases; mortality denominator: population**
Deaths attributed to disease ÷ all deaths = proportionate mortality, not mortality rate
Cross-sectional surveys cannot directly establish incidence or temporal causation

table.title: Independent examples
rows: Current cases ÷ population at one time
New outbreak cases ÷ exposed at-risk people

measures-of-disease-frequency.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist
Effective communication: bedside verbal handoff with patient → real-time feedback, shared mental model

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors
Do not trust result delivery alone (fax, mail); **test-tracking log** verifies receipt, review, follow-up

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back

table.title: Event classification
rows: Unanticipated death/serious harm/life-saving rescue; prompts RCA
Upstream scheduling/staffing flaw; fix system, not individual

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.evidence: Not checked online; established patient-safety terminology and ethical disclosure principles.

meningitis.name: Meningitis
meningitis.scope: Bacterial meningitis, viral meningitis, fungal/cryptococcal meningitis, CSF interpretation, empiric antimicrobial therapy, chemoprophylaxis
meningitis.core: Fever, headache and meningeal symptoms require prompt CSF evaluation when safe; suspected bacterial meningitis demands antibiotics without imaging-related delay.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adults: **S. pneumoniae** most common; seeded by pneumonia, otitis, sinusitis, CSF leak, asplenia
Neonates: GBS, E. coli, Listeria; older adults/immunocompromised: additional Listeria risk
Crowding/asplenia → meningococcus; advanced HIV/transplant/chemotherapy → Cryptococcus

rows.label: Clues
items: Neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting; infants may show poor feeding, irritability or bulging fontanelle
★ Petechiae/purpura with shock → **meningococcemia**; absence of rash does not exclude
Confusion, seizure or focal deficit raises encephalitis, raised-pressure or complicated infection concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Organisms reach meninges hematogenously or through contiguous spread/CSF defect; inflammation increases edema and pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Blood cultures → LP** with opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain/culture and PCR
CT before LP for focal deficit, papilledema, new seizure, marked consciousness impairment or significant immunocompromise
★ If LP delayed: cultures then **immediate antibiotics**; CT cannot rule out every pressure hazard
Cryptococcus: subacute, high opening pressure ± CN VI palsy, CSF antigen; TB studies if lymphocytic, low glucose

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult empiric → **vancomycin + ceftriaxone**; add ampicillin if >50 or immunocompromised
Neonate → ampicillin + cefotaxime; avoid ceftriaxone in neonates
Dexamethasone before/with first antibiotic when pneumococcal meningitis suspected; narrow treatment by organism
Cryptococcal meningitis → liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole; serial therapeutic LPs for pressure
Uncomplicated viral meningitis → supportive care; suspected HSV encephalitis → IV acyclovir

rows.label: Complications
items: Hearing loss, seizures, hydrocephalus, stroke, cognitive impairment; meningococcus → DIC/adrenal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Meningococcal contacts within 7 days of onset → **rifampin or ceftriaxone**; droplet isolation until 24 hours treated
Hib prophylaxis for qualifying households/childcare; no routine pneumococcal contact antibiotics
Pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccination; correct recurrent CSF leaks

rows.label: Mimics
items: SAH: thunderclap headache; CT/LP hemorrhagic findings
Encephalitis: parenchymal dysfunction, focal deficits or prominent behavioral change

meningitis.evidence: Contact prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [CDC meningococcal guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/surv-manual/php/table-of-contents/chapter-8-meningococcal-disease.html); empiric regimens established teaching.

menopause.name: Menopause
menopause.scope: Perimenopause, menopause transition, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, HRT
menopause.core: Menopause is 12 months without menses from ovarian follicle depletion; manage bothersome symptoms according to uterine status and hormone-treatment risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Natural transition typically in late 40s–50s; smoking, oophorectomy, chemotherapy or pelvic radiation accelerate onset
Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency and requires a separate evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Perimenopause: variable cycles, skipped periods, fertility remains; isolated irregularity → **reassurance**, no biopsy
Vasomotor episodes: abrupt heat, flushing, sweating, disturbed sleep; mood symptoms can coexist
Genitourinary syndrome: dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency and recurrent UTIs; pale thin friable mucosa
Urogenital estrogen loss: **negative cultures**, possible sterile pyuria; friable mucosa → spotting, postcoital bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ↓Follicles → ↓estradiol/inhibin and ↑FSH; hypothalamic thermoregulatory changes drive hot flashes
Urogenital estrogen deficiency thins epithelium, raises vaginal pH and changes flora

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms at **≥45 years → clinical diagnosis**; routine FSH unnecessary
Unexpected amenorrhea → pregnancy test; earlier menopause → FSH/estradiol and targeted thyroid/prolactin evaluation
Postmenopausal bleeding → endometrial evaluation; do not attribute to normal transition
Hormonal contraception alters bleeding/FSH interpretation; amenorrhea on contraception alone does not establish menopause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Bothersome hot flashes, low risk, generally <60 or within 10 years → **systemic estrogen**
★ Intact uterus → **add progestogen**; hysterectomy → estrogen alone usually sufficient
Avoid systemic hormones with unexplained bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancer, prior VTE/stroke/MI or active liver disease
Hormones unsuitable → **venlafaxine, paroxetine or gabapentin**; selected fezolinetant requires liver monitoring
★ Isolated GSM → lubricants/moisturizers then **low-dose vaginal estrogen**; routine progestogen generally unnecessary

rows.label: Complications
items: Bone loss, fracture, sexual dysfunction; oral systemic estrogen increases VTE/stroke risk
Combined systemic hormones can increase breast cancer risk; unopposed uterine estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium/vitamin D, smoking cessation; age/risk-based osteoporosis screening
Hormone treatment not for primary cardiovascular/dementia prevention; reassess symptoms and risks periodically
Continue contraception during transition until menopause criteria met; menopausal hormones do not prevent pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent heat intolerance, tachycardia, suppressed TSH
Pregnancy: positive hCG despite irregular cycles

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

mittelschmerz.name: Mittelschmerz
mittelschmerz.scope: Physiologic midcycle pain, follicular enlargement and rupture, timing (days 10-14 of 28-day cycle), unilateral lower quadrant pain, differentiation from surgical abdomen, reassurance
mittelschmerz.core: Brief unilateral lower-abdominal pain around ovulation, without fever or systemic illness, suggests benign mittelschmerz after urgent causes are excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory menstrual cycles; recurrence may track cycle timing, without alternating sides predictably

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Timing around **days 10–14 of a 28-day cycle**; varies with cycle length
Mild focal tenderness, occasional scant spotting; resolves within hours, sometimes up to 48 hours
★ **Persistent/worsening pain, fever, vomiting, syncope, guarding** → investigate urgent alternatives

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Follicular expansion stretches ovarian capsule; follicular fluid or small blood release irritates peritoneum

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test** in reproductive-age acute pelvic pain, even with reported normal menses
Classic recurrent, self-limited pattern with reassuring examination → clinical diagnosis
Atypical/severe symptoms → pelvic ultrasound; examine for adnexal mass, torsion signs, or significant free fluid
Small physiologic pelvic fluid may be normal; neither confirms diagnosis nor excludes an emergency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance**, local heat, acetaminophen or brief NSAID course for bothersome symptoms
Recurrent disabling episodes without pregnancy goal → combined hormonal contraception to suppress ovulation
Trying to conceive → discuss analgesic choice and fertile timing; ovulation suppression conflicts with fertility goal
No antibiotics or surgery for a confidently established benign episode

rows.label: Complications
items: No expected long-term organ damage; main hazard is misattributing ectopic pregnancy, torsion, or appendicitis
Repeated severe pain despite suppression warrants reassessment rather than indefinite symptomatic labeling

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cycle/symptom diary clarifies recurrence; hormonal suppression prevents episodes when desired and medically suitable

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, pregnancy of unknown location, possible instability
Ovarian torsion: abrupt severe pain, nausea/vomiting, enlarged ovary; normal flow does not exclude
Appendicitis: progressive pain, anorexia, focal peritoneal signs independent of cycle

mittelschmerz.evidence: Not checked online; established benign ovulatory-pain and acute-pelvic-pain teaching.

mononeuropathies.name: Mononeuropathies
mononeuropathies.scope: Ulnar nerve entrapment (cubital tunnel, Guyon canal, claw hand), radial nerve palsy (wrist drop, Saturday night palsy), peroneal/fibular nerve injury (foot drop), electromyography, splinting, surgical decompression
mononeuropathies.core: Weakness and sensory loss following one peripheral nerve suggest focal compression or injury; preserved muscles supplied proximally help localize the lesion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Compression, fractures, repetitive motion, tight casts, diabetes; intoxicated immobilization → Saturday night radial palsy
Prolonged elbow flexion, cycling/hypothenar pressure, leg crossing, rapid weight loss
Lithotomy/hip hyperflexion → **femoral** under inguinal ligament; stirrup at fibular head → foot drop
Antecubital hematoma after venipuncture → **median at elbow**; hook of hamate fracture → ulnar in Guyon canal

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Ulnar: **Froment sign**, advanced fourth/fifth-digit clawing; impaired grip and fine finger tasks
Rapid progression, severe pain, multiple noncontiguous nerves → consider vasculitic mononeuritis multiplex
Supraspinatus/infraspinatus atrophy, sensation intact, overhead athlete → **suprascapular** entrapment
Medial plantar laceration → medial toe hyperextension; superficial radial → dorsal web numbness, no wrist drop

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Focal compression first causes conduction block/demyelination; severe or sustained pressure causes axonal loss
Axonal regeneration is slow; duration and severity predict recovery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Map strength, reflexes, and sensation; compare muscles sharing a root but supplied by different nerves
Persistent/uncertain deficit → **EMG/nerve conduction studies**; denervation may take weeks to appear
Trauma → radiographs; suspected mass/structural entrapment → ultrasound or MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove compression; activity modification, **splinting**, occupational/physical rehabilitation
Ulnar at elbow → night extension splint; radial palsy → wrist-extension splint
Foot drop → ankle-foot orthosis and gait training; inspect cast/brace pressure points
★ Progressive deficit/refractory entrapment → **surgical decompression**; nerve laceration → urgent repair evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Muscle atrophy, fixed contractures, chronic neuropathic pain, falls
Delayed recognition of ongoing compression → irreversible motor deficit

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid prolonged elbow pressure, excessive flexion, leg crossing; pad vulnerable areas during surgery/immobility
Optimize diabetes control; ergonomic adjustment and frequent position changes

rows.label: Mimics
items: L5 radiculopathy: root-pattern pain; weakness also in tibialis posterior and gluteus medius
C8 radiculopathy: additional median-innervated muscle weakness, proximal symptoms
Stroke: sudden deficit with upper motor neuron signs or additional central findings

table.title: Localize common lesions
rows: Ulnar hand intrinsics; forearm spared; wrist Tinel
Palmar ulnar digits; dorsal hand spared
Finger extension; wrist extension partly preserved

mononeuropathies.evidence: Not checked online; established peripheral nerve localization and management.

mood-stabilizers.name: Mood stabilizers
mood-stabilizers.scope: Lithium (therapeutic range, toxicity, hemodialysis, tremor, nephrogenic DI, hypothyroidism), valproate (hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, teratogenicity), carbamazepine, lamotrigine (Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
mood-stabilizers.core: Match the drug to bipolar phase; narrow therapeutic windows, organ toxicity, interactions, and pregnancy risks drive selection.

rows.label: Use
items: Lithium: mania, maintenance, reduced suicide risk; valproate/carbamazepine: acute mania
Lamotrigine: bipolar depression prevention; ineffective for acute mania

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Lithium alters intracellular signaling; anticonvulsants reduce excitatory neurotransmission

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Lithium: **nephrogenic DI**, hypothyroidism, hyperparathyroidism; fine tremor → **propranolol**
Valproate: hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, thrombocytopenia, weight gain
★ **Lamotrigine rash → stop immediately**; Stevens-Johnson risk increases with rapid titration

rows.label: Avoid
items: Valproate in pregnancy: neural tube defects, impaired neurodevelopment; carbamazepine also teratogenic
Lithium: severe renal impairment, dehydration; pregnancy counseling includes fetal cardiac risk

rows.label: Interactions
items: Thiazides, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, NSAIDs increase lithium; volume depletion worsens toxicity
Carbamazepine: CYP induction, reduced contraceptive efficacy; valproate increases lamotrigine levels

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Lithium **12-hour trough**: maintenance usually 0.6–1.0; acute mania 0.8–1.2 mEq/L
Renal function, TSH, calcium; valproate CBC/LFTs; carbamazepine CBC, sodium, LFTs
Carbamazepine: HLA-B*1502 testing with relevant Asian ancestry; agranulocytosis, SIADH, severe rash

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Lithium toxicity: coarse tremor, ataxia, confusion → stop lithium, IV saline
**Hemodialysis**: seizures/coma, life-threatening arrhythmia, or renal impairment with lithium >4 mEq/L
Consider dialysis: >5 mEq/L, confusion, or clearance >36 hours to <1; monitor rebound

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Light chains injure renal tubules; low polyclonal immunoglobulins → **encapsulated bacteria**, e.g., pneumococcus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis
Urine dipstick detects albumin, misses light chains; negative dipstick does not exclude cast nephropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasms
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.scope: CML, polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, primary myelofibrosis
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.core: Clonal marrow proliferation elevates mature blood-cell counts or causes progressive fibrosis; thrombosis and transformation drive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually acquired stem-cell mutations in adults; age and prior thrombosis predict vascular risk
Prior radiation exposure associated with CML; no common lifestyle trigger explains most cases

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, fatigue, early satiety, constitutional symptoms; markedly abnormal CBC may be incidental
★ **Aquagenic pruritus**, erythromelalgia or unexplained splanchnic thrombosis → evaluate clonal disease
Very high platelets may paradoxically cause mucosal bleeding through acquired von Willebrand dysfunction
PV with headache, visual/CNS hyperviscosity symptoms → **urgent phlebotomy** before relying on aspirin

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Constitutive tyrosine-kinase signaling produces growth independent of normal feedback
Myelofibrosis → cytokine-driven fibrosis and extramedullary hematopoiesis; not simply excess fibroblast clonality

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear**, erythropoietin with erythrocytosis; marrow biopsy and mutation testing classify disease
PV thresholds: hemoglobin >16.5 g/dL men/>16 women or hematocrit >49%/>48%, with diagnostic context
ET requires persistent platelets ≥450,000/µL plus marrow/molecular findings and exclusion of reactive causes
Teardrops and leukoerythroblastosis support fibrosis; marrow aspiration may yield dry tap

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ PV → **phlebotomy to hematocrit <45%** plus low-dose aspirin if safe
PV/ET high thrombotic risk → hydroxyurea; interferon favored for selected younger/pregnant patients
★ CML → **BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor**, e.g., imatinib; monitor molecular response
Symptomatic myelofibrosis → JAK inhibitor such as ruxolitinib; allogeneic transplant potentially curative
Extreme thrombocytosis with bleeding → assess von Willebrand function before aspirin; urgent cytoreduction if critical

rows.label: Complications
items: Arterial/venous thrombosis, hemorrhage, hyperuricemia; secondary myelofibrosis or AML
CML blast phase: ≥20% blasts; advanced disease needs acute-leukemia-directed specialist treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Cardiovascular risk control; disease-specific count control, pregnancy planning, monitor progression

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive thrombocytosis: iron deficiency/inflammation; secondary erythrocytosis: hypoxia or ↑EPO
Leukemoid reaction: toxic granulation, infection trigger, absent BCR-ABL

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

narcolepsy.name: Narcolepsy
narcolepsy.scope: Excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, hypnagogic and hypnopompic hallucinations, sleep paralysis, polysomnography and MSLT, hypocretin (orexin) deficiency, modafinil, sodium oxybate
narcolepsy.core: Irresistible sleep attacks despite sufficient nighttime sleep, with emotion-triggered loss of muscle tone strongly suggesting type 1 narcolepsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually adolescent/young-adult onset; genetic susceptibility with probable autoimmune hypothalamic neuron loss

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Cataplexy**: seconds to minutes of weakness, preserved consciousness; laughter or surprise trigger
Vivid hallucinations at sleep onset or awakening; transient inability to move at sleep transitions
Short naps refreshing; disrupted nighttime sleep; daytime automatic behaviors

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Type 1: deficient hypothalamic hypocretin/orexin → unstable wakefulness and REM intrusion
Type 2: no cataplexy, no demonstrated orexin deficiency

rows.label: Dx
items: Daily sleepiness ≥3 months; sleep diary/actigraphy first to document sufficient sleep
★ Overnight **polysomnography → next-day MSLT**; exclude untreated OSA and sleep deprivation
Mean sleep latency ≤8 minutes plus ≥2 sleep-onset REM periods; preceding PSG can contribute one
Low CSF hypocretin supports type 1; usually unnecessary with characteristic cataplexy and diagnostic testing
Coordinate stimulant/REM-suppressing drug washout before testing; abrupt withdrawal can confound results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daytime sleepiness → **modafinil**; alternatives methylphenidate, pitolisant, solriamfetol
★ Prominent cataplexy → **sodium oxybate**; venlafaxine can suppress attacks
Oxybate: avoid alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines because of respiratory/CNS depression
Scheduled naps, regular nighttime sleep, workplace/school accommodations

rows.label: Complications
items: Motor vehicle crashes, impaired school/work performance, depression
Modafinil reduces hormonal contraceptive effectiveness; review pregnancy planning

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid driving or hazardous work until sleepiness controlled; reassess driving safety during follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: OSA: snoring, witnessed apneas, abnormal respiratory PSG
Idiopathic hypersomnia: long unrefreshing sleep, fewer sleep-onset REM periods
Syncope/seizure: loss of consciousness or postictal confusion rather than isolated cataplexy

needlestick-injuries.name: Needlestick injuries and bloodborne pathogen exposure
needlestick-injuries.scope: Hepatitis B postexposure prophylaxis, HIV postexposure prophylaxis, hepatitis C monitoring, tetanus prophylaxis in puncture wounds
needlestick-injuries.core: After blood exposure, wash immediately, report promptly, assess the source and start time-sensitive prophylaxis before results if transmission risk warrants.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Deep hollow-bore injury, visibly bloody device, intravascular needle and viremic source increase transmission risk
Mucosal/nonintact skin blood contact qualifies; intact skin contact alone usually does not

rows.label: Clues
items: Often no acute symptoms; exposure history and source status determine immediate decisions
Acute fever/rash after exposure → evaluate HIV seroconversion; jaundice/transaminitis → hepatitis assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Direct inoculation bypasses epithelial barriers; early HIV replication can be interrupted before established infection
HBV vaccination establishes protective antibody; HCV lacks vaccine or proven postexposure drug prophylaxis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Source: **HIV Ag/Ab, HBsAg, HCV RNA** or anti-HCV with reflex RNA
Exposed worker baseline: HIV Ag/Ab, HBV immunity status, anti-HCV/reflex RNA; creatinine/AST/ALT for PEP
★ HIV final follow-up: **Ag/Ab + NAT at 12 weeks**; earlier testing for delayed/missed PEP
HCV follow-up if indicated: **RNA at 3–6 weeks**, anti-HCV/reflex RNA at 4–6 months

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Wash with soap/water, flush mucosa; **no squeezing, bleach or caustic antiseptics**
★ HIV PEP: start immediately, ideally hours and within **72 hours**, continue 28 days
Preferred HIV PEP: **bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide**
HIV-negative source → stop PEP unless acute infection suspected; suppressed source → individualized expert assessment
No HCV PEP; detected infection → direct-acting antiviral evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HIV/HBV/HCV acquisition, medication adverse effects, anxiety; pregnancy does not justify delaying indicated HIV PEP

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety needles, sharps containers, no recapping; pre-exposure HBV immunization with documented response
Puncture wound: tetanus booster if last dose ≥5 years or date unknown; no prophylactic antibiotics
Primary tetanus series unknown/incomplete → vaccine + TIG
Puncture + HIV/severe immunodeficiency → TIG regardless of prior tetanus vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbloody saliva/urine: no meaningful HIV exposure unless blood contamination
Community discarded needle: low/uncertain risk; individualized assessment rather than automatic risk equivalence

neonatal-resuscitation.name: Neonatal resuscitation
neonatal-resuscitation.scope: NRP algorithm, initial steps (warm, dry, stimulate), PPV indications (apnea, HR < 100), chest compressions (HR < 60), epinephrine, target SpO2
neonatal-resuscitation.core: At birth, effective ventilation drives heart-rate recovery; escalate support according to the response after each timed intervention.

rows.label: Definition
items: Apgar: appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration, each scored 0–2 at 1 and 5 min
Score 1: acrocyanosis, pulse <100, grimace, some flexion, irregular breathing

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Right-hand preductal pulse oximetry**; targets: 2 min 65–70%, 5 min 80–85%, 10 min 85–95%
Auscultate HR initially; ECG improves continuous measurement during advanced support
Oxygen start: ≥35 wk **21%**; 32–34 wk 21–30%; <32 wk 30–100%, titrated

rows.label: Use when
items: Vigorous term newborn → skin-to-skin, routine care; defer cord clamping ≥60 seconds
★ Poor tone/breathing → **warm, dry, position airway, stimulate**; initial assessment within first minute
Spontaneous breathing plus distress/cyanosis → oxygen titration; consider CPAP

rows.label: Compare
items: ★ Poor PPV → **reposition, reseal, open mouth, suction obstruction, raise pressure, alternate airway**
Compressions: two-thumb encircling technique, depth one-third chest; 90 compressions + 30 breaths/min
Epinephrine: **0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV/IO**; repeat every 3–5 min; umbilical venous access preferred

rows.label: Traps
items: No routine suction, including meconium; suction only suspected airway obstruction
★ **2025 PPV rate 30–60/min**; older teaching 40–60/min
Persistent bradycardia → check pneumothorax/hypovolemia; blood loss → saline or uncrossmatched blood

table.title: Timed escalation
rows: Stop compressions; continue ventilation if needed

nephrolithiasis.name: Nephrolithiasis
nephrolithiasis.scope: Renal colic, calcium oxalate, uric acid, struvite, cystine, drug-induced stones, noncontrast CT, medical expulsive therapy, surgical indications
nephrolithiasis.core: Sudden colicky flank pain radiating toward the groin with hematuria suggests a ureteral stone; infection plus obstruction is an emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low urine volume, high sodium intake, family history, obesity, gout
Hyperparathyroidism, malabsorption, recurrent urinary infection; low citrate, genetic defects

rows.label: Clues
items: Restlessness, nausea/vomiting, CVA tenderness; hematuria may be absent
★ **Fever, pyuria, hypotension, AKI, anuria** → infected or function-threatening obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urinary supersaturation → crystal formation; obstruction raises ureteral pressure and provokes spasm
Ileal resection/Crohn → fatty acids bind calcium → **colonic oxalate absorption** → calcium oxalate stones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + culture if infection suspected**, creatinine, pregnancy test when relevant
★ Nonpregnant adult → **low-dose noncontrast CT**; pregnancy/children → renal ultrasound first
KUB misses radiolucent uric acid stones; radiographic invisibility does not exclude ureteral obstruction
Analyze passed stone; recurrent/high-risk disease → serum evaluation and 24-hour urine

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Ketorolac** for analgesia, ondansetron for nausea, normal hydration; avoid forced high-volume fluids during obstruction
Small uncomplicated stones, pain controlled, afebrile → discharge, oral fluids, analgesia; distal 5–10 mm → consider tamsulosin
★ Infection + obstruction → **urgent stent or nephrostomy + IV antibiotics**; delay definitive stone removal
Intervene for uncontrolled pain, persistent obstruction, renal deterioration, large stone, or failed passage
Ureteroscopy/shock-wave lithotripsy selected by stone; >2 cm/staghorn → percutaneous nephrolithotomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydronephrosis, pyelonephritis/urosepsis, recurrent stones, renal loss
Procedures → bleeding, infection, ureteral injury; tamsulosin → orthostasis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Aim **urine volume ≥2–2.5 L/day**, normal dietary calcium, low sodium, moderate animal protein
Recurrent calcium stones/hypercalciuria → chlorthalidone; hypocitraturia → potassium citrate
Do not restrict dietary calcium routinely; calcium with meals reduces enteric oxalate absorption

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: older patient, hemodynamic instability, aortic dilation
Pyelonephritis: fever/constant pain; torsion/ectopic pregnancy: genital/pelvic findings

table.title: Stone clues and targeted prevention
rows: Indinavir CT-occult; atazanavir CT-visible; topiramate promotes alkaline urine

nephrolithiasis.evidence: Not checked online; established stone evaluation and prevention principles.

neurocutaneous-disorders.name: Neurocutaneous disorders
neurocutaneous-disorders.scope: Neurofibromatosis type 1, neurofibromatosis type 2, tuberous sclerosis, Sturge-Weber syndrome, von Hippel-Lindau disease, ataxia-telangiectasia
neurocutaneous-disorders.core: Characteristic skin or ocular lesions plus neurologic tumors, seizures, or progressive ataxia suggest an inherited or mosaic multisystem disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NF1, NF2-related schwannomatosis, TSC, VHL: autosomal dominant; frequent de novo variants
Ataxia-telangiectasia: autosomal recessive; Sturge-Weber: sporadic somatic mosaicism

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Changing painful neurofibroma**, rapid growth, or new weakness → malignant transformation concern
Early focal seizures or developmental regression → evaluate structural cerebral lesions
NF2: hearing loss/tinnitus; NF1: cutaneous neurofibromas and childhood learning difficulties

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor suppressor dysfunction → hamartomas or neoplasms; ATM defect → impaired DNA repair

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical pattern + genetic testing**; targeted MRI for neurologic or tumor symptoms
NF1: ≥2 criteria; ≥6 café-au-lait macules, size >5 mm prepubertal, >15 mm postpubertal
TSC: two major features or one major plus two minor; pathogenic variant also diagnostic

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic tumors → specialist resection; TSC growing lesions → **everolimus** in selected cases
TSC infantile spasms → vigabatrin; other seizures → antiseizure drugs
Sturge-Weber seizures → levetiracetam; refractory focal epilepsy → surgical evaluation
Ataxia-telangiectasia: rehabilitation, infection treatment; minimize ionizing radiation

rows.label: Complications
items: NF1: malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor; VHL: renal carcinoma and pheochromocytoma
TSC: hydrocephalus, renal hemorrhage; ataxia-telangiectasia: lymphoma/leukemia, recurrent sinopulmonary infections

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**; syndrome-specific eye, hearing, renal, and tumor surveillance
Sturge-Weber: ophthalmology follow-up for glaucoma; NF1: childhood BP and vision monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Isolated café-au-lait macules: no additional diagnostic criteria
Friedreich ataxia: areflexia, cardiomyopathy, no ocular telangiectasias

table.title: Signature findings
rows: Axillary freckling, Lisch nodules, optic glioma
Ash-leaf macules, angiofibromas, cortical tubers, renal angiomyolipomas

neurocutaneous-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical genetics teaching.

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.name: Neuromuscular junction disorders
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.scope: Myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, botulism, repetitive nerve stimulation, autoantibodies
neuromuscular-junction-disorders.core: Fluctuating or descending weakness with preserved sensation localizes to neuromuscular transmission; reflexes, pupils, and exercise response separate major causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: MG: autoimmune disease, thymoma; LEMS: smoking/small-cell lung carcinoma
Botulism: improperly canned foods, injection wounds, infant honey or environmental spores

rows.label: Clues
items: MG: diplopia, ptosis, nasal speech, chewing fatigue; worse late day or repeated activity
LEMS: proximal leg weakness, dry mouth, constipation; transient strength/reflex improvement after exertion
Botulism: cranial palsies → symmetric descending paralysis, autonomic dysfunction; infant constipation and floppy weakness
★ **Bulbar weakness or declining ventilation** → impending respiratory failure even with normal oxygen saturation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: MG: postsynaptic receptor/MuSK autoimmunity; LEMS: presynaptic voltage-gated calcium-channel autoimmunity
Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins → impaired acetylcholine release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AChR antibodies**, then MuSK if negative; repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG
MG → chest CT for thymoma; bedside ice-pack improvement supports ocular disease
LEMS → P/Q calcium-channel antibodies and chest CT for cancer
★ Suspected crisis → serial **forced vital capacity/negative inspiratory force**; not pulse oximetry alone
Botulism → serum/stool/toxin testing via public health; treatment before confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: MG → pyridostigmine, steroid-sparing immunosuppression; thymectomy for thymoma or selected generalized AChR-positive disease
★ Myasthenic crisis → **airway support + IVIG or plasma exchange**, treat precipitant
LEMS → amifampridine and treatment of malignancy; immunotherapy for persistent autoimmune disease
★ Botulism → **heptavalent antitoxin**; infants → human botulism immune globulin; ventilatory support
Wound botulism → debridement/antibiotics; avoid aminoglycosides and magnesium with impaired junctional transmission

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, respiratory arrest; MG immunosuppression → infection; steroids may initially worsen weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review MG-exacerbating drugs; safe food preservation; no honey before age 1 year
LEMS → ongoing cancer surveillance if initial evaluation negative

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: usually ascending weakness and areflexia, possible sensory symptoms
Brainstem stroke: abrupt focal signs; motor neuron disease: fasciculations/UMN signs

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.evidence: Botulism checked 2026-10-30: [CDC clinical guidelines](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/70/rr/rr7002a1.htm); MG/LEMS: established teaching.

neutropenia.name: Neutropenia
neutropenia.scope: Benign ethnic neutropenia (Duffy-null), drug-induced neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, autoimmune neutropenia, ANC thresholds, evaluation and management
neutropenia.core: Infection risk tracks the depth and duration of neutrophil depletion; fever with severe neutropenia is an antibiotic emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cytotoxic chemotherapy, marrow malignancy, viral infection, autoimmune disease, B12/folate/copper deficiency
Clozapine, methimazole, propylthiouracil, TMP–SMX and other drugs can cause agranulocytosis
Duffy-null associated neutrophil counts: stable isolated reduction without increased infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcers, gingivitis, recurrent bacterial/fungal infections; inflammatory signs and pus may be absent
Cyclic mouth ulcers/infections suggest cyclic neutropenia; multiple cytopenias suggest marrow disease
Drug-associated fever or sore throat → urgent CBC, especially with antithyroid drugs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced marrow production, peripheral destruction or splenic sequestration lowers circulating neutrophils
Mucosal barrier injury plus impaired innate defense permits rapid invasive bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANC = WBC × (% neutrophils + bands)/100**; repeat CBC with differential and smear
Mild: 1000–1500/µL; moderate: 500–1000; **severe <500**; profound <100
★ Febrile neutropenia: **≥38.3°C once or ≥38.0°C for ≥1 hour**, ANC <500 or expected decline
Obtain peripheral/line blood cultures, targeted cultures and imaging without delaying antibiotics
Persistent unexplained severe counts, abnormal smear or other cytopenias → marrow evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Febrile severe neutropenia → **IV cefepime**, piperacillin–tazobactam or meropenem promptly
Add vancomycin for shock, suspected line/skin infection, pneumonia or documented resistant gram-positive infection
★ Stop culprit drug; G-CSF for selected severe/drug-related cases and high-risk chemotherapy settings
Carefully selected low-risk stable patients → oral ciprofloxacin + amoxicillin–clavulanate with reliable close follow-up
High-risk persistent fever 4–7 days → fungal evaluation and empiric **caspofungin**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas sepsis, invasive candidiasis/aspergillosis, neutropenic enterocolitis; avoid rectal instrumentation
**Ecthyma gangrenosum**: bulla → painless black necrotic ulcer, Pseudomonas bacteremia; antipseudomonal drug, not steroids

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, oral care; selected prolonged profound neutropenia → antibacterial/antifungal prophylaxis
Stable Duffy-null pattern → reassurance after excluding other causes; no unnecessary G-CSF

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lymphopenia: opportunistic infection risk with preserved ANC
Acute leukemia: blasts and additional cytopenias

obsessive-compulsive-disorder.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.scope: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, ego-dystonic obsessions and compulsions, exposure and response prevention, SSRIs
obsessive-compulsive-disorder.core: Intrusive unwanted thoughts and ritualized acts consume time or impair function; treatment breaks the cycle of anxiety and neutralization.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Often begins in childhood/adolescence; family history, tic disorders, anxiety/depression comorbidity
Stress may worsen symptoms; intrusive harm/sexual thoughts do not alone imply intent

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Ego-dystonic obsessions**: contamination, doubt, symmetry, aggressive or taboo thoughts
Compulsions: washing, checking, counting or mental rituals aimed at preventing feared outcomes
Usually recognizes excessiveness, but insight ranges to absent; reassurance seeking can function as a ritual
Skin injury from washing, lateness or avoidance; severe cases markedly restrict eating or daily activity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical dysfunction; rituals transiently reduce distress and are negatively reinforced

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical interview**: obsessions/compulsions >1 hour daily or significant distress/impairment
Assess insight, functional effect, suicidality, tics and depression; Yale-Brown scale tracks severity
Exclude substances/medical causes and distinguish repetitive behaviors driven by other disorders

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT with exposure and response prevention**: graded feared-stimulus exposure without ritual completion
★ **SSRI**, e.g., sertraline/fluoxetine; mild-moderate pediatric OCD → ERP alone first; substantial impairment → combine
Often higher tolerated SSRI doses and 8–12-week trial needed; do not label failure after brief exposure
Persistent symptoms → optimize ERP/adherence, switch SSRI or clomipramine; selected resistant disease → risperidone
Reduce family accommodation/reassurance rituals; maintain effective treatment before gradual taper

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, suicidality, social/occupational disability; dermatitis from compulsive washing
Clomipramine → anticholinergic effects, arrhythmia and overdose risk; SSRI → sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Generalized anxiety: realistic everyday worries rather than intrusive obsession/neutralization cycle
Psychosis: fixed belief without typical resisted ritual; assess insight carefully

table.title: Related repetitive patterns
rows: Developmental social differences, soothing stereotyped routines
Brief involuntary movement/sound with premonitory urge

opioid-toxicity.name: Opioid toxicity
opioid-toxicity.scope: Opioid toxidrome, naloxone administration and titration, observation period, precipitated withdrawal
opioid-toxicity.core: Depressed consciousness, slow breathing, and pinpoint pupils after opioid exposure; ventilation takes priority over full awakening.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fentanyl or heroin exposure, dose escalation, renal dysfunction, long-acting opioids
Alcohol/benzodiazepine co-ingestion; lost tolerance after detoxification, hospitalization, or incarceration

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Bradypnea or apnea** with hypoxemia; reduced bowel sounds, bradycardia, hypotension
Miosis may be absent with severe hypoxia or co-ingestion; needle marks are not required
Pulmonary edema, aspiration, hypothermia, prolonged immobilization may accompany overdose
Chronic use: daytime sleepiness, constipation, apathy, falling grades, miosis, slow breathing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mu-receptor activation suppresses medullary ventilatory response to CO2
Naloxone competitively reverses opioid effects but often wears off before the causative opioid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; bedside glucose, pulse oximetry, capnography; do not await toxicology
Urine opiate immunoassay detects morphine/heroin/codeine; may miss fentanyl, methadone, and oxycodone
ECG for methadone-associated QT prolongation; acetaminophen level with uncertain combination-product ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open airway, **bag-mask ventilation**, oxygen; intubate if ventilation cannot be maintained
★ **Naloxone** IV titrated to adequate breathing; intranasal/IM route if IV unavailable
Dependent but breathing: start low; apnea/no response: prompt larger/repeated doses, especially fentanyl analogs
Repeated recurrence → naloxone infusion; coma despite repeated doses → evaluate additional causes
Short-acting reversal: observe ≥4 hours after last naloxone; long-acting/recurrent sedation → prolonged monitoring/admission

rows.label: Complications
items: Anoxic brain injury, aspiration pneumonia, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome
Precipitated withdrawal: agitation, vomiting, diarrhea, tachycardia; rare pulmonary edema after reversal

rows.label: Prevention
items: Take-home naloxone, overdose-response training, avoid sedative combinations; offer buprenorphine and addiction follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pontine hemorrhage: focal neurologic findings, no meaningful naloxone response
Clonidine poisoning: marked bradycardia with similar pupils
Sedative overdose: usually normal pupils; incomplete naloxone response

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, **obesity** (strongest modifiable), prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain, severe or worsening: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; not an OA flare; mild cool effusion → x-ray, simple analgesic
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen if unable to use NSAIDs (older exam questions may expect it first); duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Weight loss** best prevents knee OA, beyond exercise alone; conditioning, injury prevention; no complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis, marginal erosions, DIP spared
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture
Trochanteric bursitis: lateral hip pain over greater trochanter, not groin pain

osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

osteomyelitis.name: Osteomyelitis
osteomyelitis.scope: Vertebral osteomyelitis and discitis, hematogenous seeding (S. aureus, IV drug use), contiguous spread (diabetic foot ulcer), probe-to-bone test, MRI, bone biopsy and culture, parenteral antibiotics
osteomyelitis.core: Persistent focal bone or back pain, especially with bacteremia, a deep diabetic ulcer, or elevated inflammatory markers, suggests bone infection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hematogenous seeding: S. aureus, endocarditis, injection drug use; vertebral disease often lacks fever
Contiguous spread: diabetic foot ulcers, pressure injury; direct inoculation: open fracture, surgery, hardware
Sickle cell: Salmonella association, but S. aureus remains important; plantar puncture through shoe → Pseudomonas

rows.label: Clues
items: Point tenderness, swelling, drainage or nonhealing sinus; systemic toxicity may be absent
★ New neurologic deficit, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention → **epidural extension/cord compression**
Diabetic ulcer over bony prominence, visible bone, or prolonged failure to heal increases suspicion
Child: fever, point tenderness over long-bone **metaphysis**; septic joint instead limits joint motion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Infected bone develops inflammatory pressure, vascular compromise, and necrosis
Sequestrum: devitalized infected bone; involucrum: reactive new bone; biofilm promotes hardware persistence

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, ESR/CRP, two blood-culture sets; plain films first but early findings can be absent
★ Diabetic foot: **probe-to-bone** plus radiographs/inflammatory markers; MRI if diagnosis remains uncertain
★ **MRI** best for early marrow disease and epidural/paraspinal abscess; bone scan uptake if MRI unavailable
Bone biopsy for histology/culture before antibiotics if stable; superficial wound swabs unreliable
Compatible vertebral MRI plus S. aureus bacteremia usually obviates biopsy; assess endocarditis source

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis or neurologic compromise → cultures then **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, urgent surgical assessment
Stable vertebral disease → obtain microbiologic diagnosis before empiric antibiotics
MSSA → cefazolin/nafcillin; MRSA → vancomycin; tailor to cultures, usually about **6 weeks**
IV initially for serious disease; selected stable patients can complete highly bioavailable oral regimens
Debride necrotic bone/drain abscess; surgery for instability, progressive deficit, or uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Epidural abscess, pathologic fracture, deformity, bacteremia, chronic draining sinus
Longstanding sinus may develop squamous carcinoma; prolonged antibiotics → line infection, renal injury, C. difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Diabetic foot inspection, offloading, vascular assessment, glucose control; prompt open-fracture antibiotics and debridement

rows.label: Mimics
items: Charcot arthropathy: neuropathic warm foot, joint fragmentation; MRI/biopsy may distinguish overlapping infection
Bone malignancy: destructive mass, pathology without infection
Degenerative disc disease: mechanical pain without infectious endplate/disc pattern

osteonecrosis.name: Osteonecrosis
osteonecrosis.scope: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, risk factors (corticosteroids, alcohol, sickle cell, trauma), MRI sensitivity, crescent sign on plain radiograph, core decompression, joint replacement
osteonecrosis.core: Progressive deep hip or groin pain after steroid exposure, heavy alcohol use, sickle cell disease, or trauma suggests femoral-head ischemia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Glucocorticoids**, excessive alcohol, sickle cell vaso-occlusion, femoral neck fracture or hip dislocation
SLE, transplantation, decompression exposure; bilateral disease common with systemic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight-bearing pain progressing to rest/night pain; limited internal rotation and abduction
Antalgic gait, referred thigh/knee pain; early examination can be nearly normal
Sudden worsening suggests subchondral fracture or articular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Interrupted subchondral blood supply → osteocyte death, microfractures, eventual joint surface collapse
Repair cannot keep pace with mechanical loading; secondary degenerative arthritis follows

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP pelvis and lateral hip radiographs** first; early disease may be radiographically occult
★ Persistent suspicion despite normal films → **MRI**, most sensitive early test
Later films: patchy sclerosis/lucency; crescent sign indicates subchondral fracture, then flattening
Evaluate contralateral hip when symptoms or systemic risk suggest bilateral involvement

rows.label: Tx
items: Protected weight-bearing, cane/crutches, NSAIDs, orthopedic referral; analgesics do not restore perfusion
★ Before collapse → **core decompression** in selected symptomatic lesions; joint-preserving options depend on extent
Advanced collapse or secondary arthritis → total hip arthroplasty
Reduce avoidable steroid/alcohol exposure; manage sickle cell and other underlying disorders

rows.label: Complications
items: Femoral-head collapse, painful osteoarthritis, loss of mobility and function
Arthroplasty: infection, dislocation, loosening; younger patients may require revision

rows.label: Prevention
items: Use lowest effective glucocorticoid exposure; counsel against heavy alcohol consumption
Prompt reduction of traumatic hip dislocation limits ischemic time; monitor high-risk post-traumatic hips
Activity modification during evaluation reduces loading on vulnerable subchondral bone

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hip osteoarthritis: gradual activity pain, joint-space narrowing and osteophytes rather than early isolated necrosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe pain with passive motion; urgent aspiration
Femoral neck stress fracture: overuse, fracture line or marrow edema on MRI
Osteomyelitis: fever, elevated ESR/CRP; osteonecrosis markers usually normal

osteonecrosis.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic diagnosis and stage-based treatment.

ovarian-cancer.name: Ovarian cancer
ovarian-cancer.scope: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma, CA-125, pelvic ultrasound, peritoneal carcinomatosis, germ cell tumors, sex cord-stromal tumors, surgical staging and cytoreduction, platinum-based chemotherapy
ovarian-cancer.core: Persistent bloating, early satiety, pelvic symptoms, or an adnexal mass—especially after menopause—requires evaluation for an often late-presenting malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, nulliparity, BRCA1/2 or Lynch syndrome; family history of breast/ovarian cancer
Endometriosis associated with clear-cell/endometrioid subtypes; pregnancy and combined contraceptives reduce epithelial risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Older patient + ascites, large/fixed pelvic mass, weight loss, pleural effusion, obstruction → **epithelial** carcinoma
Young patient with rapidly enlarging mass → germ cell tumor; estrogen/androgen effects → stromal tumor
Postmenopausal bleeding with adnexal mass → consider estrogen-secreting granulosa tumor and endometrial disease
★ **Palpable ovary after menopause** → abnormal (ovaries atrophy); pelvic ultrasound

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Many high-grade serous tumors arise in distal fallopian tube epithelium
Transcoelomic seeding produces peritoneal/omental disease; hormone secretion depends on tumor lineage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transvaginal ultrasound** first; solid components, papillary projections, vascularity, ascites increase suspicion
★ **CA-125** supports risk assessment/monitoring, not diagnosis or average-risk screening
Young/complex mass → β-hCG, AFP, LDH; suspected stromal tumor → inhibin/sex hormones
Suspected malignancy → CT abdomen/pelvis/chest and gynecologic oncology; definitive histology and staging usually surgical
Isolated resectable mass → avoid aspiration; advanced disease → biopsy before neoadjuvant chemotherapy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Epithelial carcinoma → **surgical staging/cytoreduction + carboplatin/paclitaxel** according to stage
Poor upfront surgical candidate → tissue confirmation, neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy, interval cytoreduction
Germ cell malignancy → fertility-sparing surgery when feasible; stage IA dysgerminoma may avoid chemotherapy
Higher-risk germ cell tumors → bleomycin/etoposide/cisplatin
Selected BRCA/HRD-associated disease → PARP-inhibitor maintenance after platinum response

rows.label: Complications
items: Peritoneal carcinomatosis, ascites, malignant obstruction, VTE; chemotherapy neuropathy/myelosuppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **No routine CA-125/ultrasound screening** in asymptomatic average-risk patients
Genetic counseling/testing; hereditary high-risk patients → discuss risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy after childbearing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endometrioma: cyclic pain, ground-glass ultrasound; CA-125 can rise
Meigs syndrome: benign ovarian fibroma plus ascites/pleural effusion; no peritoneal implants

table.title: Tumor markers
rows: Often bilateral; psammoma bodies; WT1+, p53 abnormal

ovarian-cysts.name: Ovarian cysts
ovarian-cysts.scope: Follicular cyst, corpus luteum cyst, theca lutein cyst (hyperstimulation), mature cystic teratoma (dermoid), unilocular vs multilocular, surveillance intervals, cystectomy indications, cyst rupture
ovarian-cysts.core: Most reproductive-age ovarian cysts are benign; morphology, symptoms, menopausal status, and persistence determine observation versus surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory cycles, early pregnancy; ovulation induction → **hyperstimulated ovaries**; very high hCG → bilateral enlargement
Postmenopausal adnexal masses carry higher malignancy risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental mass, pelvic pressure, unilateral discomfort; sudden pain after intercourse/exertion suggests rupture
★ Sudden severe pain with vomiting → **torsion**; syncope/hypotension → major intraperitoneal bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Functional lesions arise during ovulation; dermoids contain differentiated germ-cell tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pregnancy test first; **transvaginal ultrasound** characterizes wall, septations, solid elements, flow, free fluid
Simple unilocular: thin wall, anechoic, no solid vascular component; multiloculation warrants closer characterization
Papillary/solid vascular components, thick septa, ascites → malignancy evaluation; CA-125 nonspecific premenopausally
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; urgent clinical concern overrides reassuring imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable functional/hemorrhagic cyst → analgesia, recheck after menses; unresolved → repeat ultrasound in **6–12 weeks**
Asymptomatic simple cyst above 5–7 cm premenopause, 3–5 cm postmenopause → ultrasound around 6–12 months
★ Hemodynamic instability → IV fluids/blood and urgent laparoscopy; torsion → detorsion with ovarian preservation
Persistent/enlarging, symptomatic, large, suspicious mass → surgery/referral
OCPs do not hasten functional-cyst resolution; older exam questions may expect OCP + 6-week recheck

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemoperitoneum, ovarian infarction, reduced ovarian reserve after surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Ovulation suppression may reduce new functional cyst formation; counsel urgent reassessment for acute pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with pregnancy outside uterus
Tubo-ovarian abscess: fever, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory complex mass

table.title: Cyst identities
rows: Luteal/early pregnancy; tender mass, crenulated vascular wall, hemorrhage
Bilateral multicystic ovaries; regress as hCG falls
Young; complex echogenic mass; fat, teeth, calcification

ovarian-cysts.evidence: Simple-cyst thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [SRU 2019 consensus](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.2019191354); acute management established teaching.

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea permissible despite risks; reassess sedation/respiration
Codeine fails → morphine/oxycodone; pain mimics depression; wears off early → shorten interval

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids**, short-acting for breakthrough; constipation → keep dose, add stimulant laxative

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals
Advanced dementia refusing intake → comfort hand-feeding by mouth; no tubes or IV

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Hospice: unrelated conditions remain treatable; no DNR requirement; enrollment revocable if goals change
