Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

table.title: Early and routine pregnancy calls
rows: Nausea, irregular bleeding or amenorrhea, even premenarche
Missed menses, urinary frequency, friable cervix, enlarged uterus
Brief sharp movement-triggered lower-quadrant pain, normal vitals
No added preterm, fluid, or placental risk

salicylate-toxicity.name: Salicylate toxicity
salicylate-toxicity.scope: Aspirin overdose, mixed respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, urinary alkalinization, hemodialysis indications
salicylate-toxicity.core: Aspirin exposure with tinnitus, tachypnea, fever, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis–anion-gap metabolic acidosis; normal pH can conceal severe poisoning.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose; chronic excess aspirin or bismuth subsalicylate, especially with renal impairment
Enteric-coated preparations or bezoars → delayed peak concentrations; older adults vulnerable to chronic toxicity

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis; confusion, seizures, hypoxemia or hyperpyrexia signal severe toxicity
Children may have predominantly metabolic acidosis; chronic exposure may resemble delirium or sepsis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medullary respiratory stimulation + oxidative phosphorylation uncoupling → hyperventilation, organic acids, heat generation
Acidemia increases nonionized salicylate → CNS entry; glucose utilization rises despite normal serum glucose

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serial salicylate levels**, ABG/VBG, electrolytes/anion gap, glucose, creatinine; check acetaminophen co-ingestion
Repeat concentrations until declining with clinical improvement; one early low level cannot exclude poisoning
★ **Severity overrides the level**; falling serum concentration with worsening acidemia can reflect tissue redistribution

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway assessment, IV fluids, potassium correction; activated charcoal early if airway protected
★ **IV sodium bicarbonate** → serum/urine alkalinization; target urine pH 7.5–8; maintain potassium
★ **Hemodialysis**: altered mentation, oxygen-requiring lung injury, failed alkalinization, or pH ≤7.20
Dialyze if level >100 mg/dL; >90 mg/dL with impaired renal function; chronic toxicity needs lower thresholds
★ Intubation only if essential; **maintain hyperventilation**; neuroglycopenia → dextrose despite normal blood glucose

rows.label: Complications
items: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, cerebral edema, renal failure, hypoglycemia, death
Sedation or inadequate ventilation → rapid acidemia and cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid aspirin for childhood viral illness; secure medications; reconcile OTC salicylate-containing products
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment and suicide safety planning after medical stabilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious source; may share respiratory alkalosis and lactic acidosis
DKA: marked ketonemia and insulin deficiency; absent salicylate exposure
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap early; methanol visual injury or ethylene glycol oxalate nephropathy

salicylate-toxicity.evidence: Dialysis thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP salicylate recommendations](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/salicylates); other management: established toxicology teaching.

salivary-gland-disorders.name: Salivary gland disorders
salivary-gland-disorders.scope: Acute suppurative sialadenitis, sialolithiasis, mumps parotitis, salivary tumors
salivary-gland-disorders.core: Salivary swelling may reflect infection, obstructed flow, viral parotitis, or a neoplasm; meal association, duct drainage, and focality guide the branch.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, postoperative state, poor oral hygiene, anticholinergic drugs reduce salivary flow
Submandibular gland predisposed to stones; unvaccinated close-contact exposure favors mumps
Prior radiation and smoking increase selected salivary tumor risks; older age raises neoplasm concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Purulence from Stensen or Wharton duct** supports acute bacterial sialadenitis
Painful unilateral gland with fever; airway symptoms, trismus, toxic appearance → deep infection/abscess
★ **Facial weakness, fixation, rapid growth**, cervical nodes with parotid mass → malignancy warning
Dry eyes/dry mouth and recurrent bilateral swelling suggest autoimmune sicca disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis permits ascending oral bacteria; S aureus common in suppurative infection
Ductal calculus blocks secretion; mumps causes viral gland inflammation; most parotid tumors benign

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Examine oral ducts and facial nerve; **ultrasound** first for stone or focal gland lesion
Contrast CT for abscess/deep extension; culture expressed pus if present
Mumps suspicion → buccal swab RT-PCR, public health notification; serology supplements selected cases
★ Persistent solid mass → **fine-needle aspiration**, imaging and ENT assessment; avoid open diagnostic biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suppurative disease → **hydration, warm compresses, gland massage, sialogogues + amoxicillin-clavulanate**
Systemic toxicity/poor oral intake → admit, IV ampicillin-sulbactam; abscess → drainage
Obstruction → stimulate flow and remove persistent stone via sialendoscopy or selected surgery
Mumps → analgesia/hydration, isolate through 5 days after swelling onset; no antibiotic benefit
Tumor → specialist surgical excision; avoid simple enucleation of pleomorphic adenoma

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, deep neck infection, recurrent sialadenitis; parotid surgery → facial nerve injury, gustatory sweating
Mumps → orchitis, meningitis, pancreatitis, hearing loss; longstanding pleomorphic adenoma may transform

rows.label: Prevention
items: Oral hygiene, hydration, minimize xerogenic drugs; MMR vaccination for mumps prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dental abscess: focal tooth tenderness, odontogenic collection
Sjögren syndrome: chronic sicca, autoimmune features rather than acute ductal pus

table.title: Presentation patterns
rows: Unilateral meal-triggered painful swelling; obstructive sialadenitis
Older smoker; sometimes bilateral parotid masses

salivary-gland-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established salivary disease and mumps isolation teaching.

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

shoulder-pain.name: Shoulder pain
shoulder-pain.scope: Rotator cuff tendinopathy and tear, impingement, adhesive capsulitis, dislocation, biceps tendinopathy, glenohumeral osteoarthritis
shoulder-pain.core: Active versus passive range of motion, true weakness, trauma history, and pain location distinguish major shoulder disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Overhead work/sports, repetitive lifting, aging; fall or traction → acute structural injury
Diabetes, thyroid disease, prolonged immobilization → capsular fibrosis
Seizure/electrocution → posterior dislocation; anterior instability follows abduction/external rotation injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Lateral upper-arm pain often shoulder origin; radiation below elbow suggests cervical source
Night pain with preserved passive motion suggests cuff disease; weakness persisting after analgesia suggests tear
★ **Fever, hot joint, severe pain with any motion** → urgent septic arthritis evaluation
★ Deformity, absent pulse, deltoid numbness → dislocation with possible neurovascular injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tendon degeneration/tearing impairs dynamic stabilization; capsule contracture restricts joint excursion
Loss of articular cartilage causes mechanically painful glenohumeral degeneration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs** for trauma, arthritis, deformity; include axillary or scapular-Y view for dislocation
Compare strength, provocative tests, neck examination; document axillary nerve and distal pulses
Ultrasound or MRI for suspected tear, persistent symptoms, or surgical planning; avoid routine immediate MRI
Supraspinatus: pain on **empty-can** (resisted abduction, internal rotation); pain felt over deltoid
Proximal biceps rupture: sudden tender anterior arm bulge after heavy lifting, painful elbow flexion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Most atraumatic disorders → **activity modification, NSAIDs, physical therapy**; HF, CAD or CKD → therapy without NSAIDs
Selected painful tendinopathy/capsulitis → corticosteroid injection; avoid repeated injections into tendons
★ Dislocation → **prompt closed reduction**, brief sling, rehabilitation; recheck neurovascular function afterward
Acute traumatic full-thickness tear with functional loss → early orthopedic referral; severe OA → arthroplasty consideration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent instability, axillary nerve injury, greater-tuberosity fracture, persistent weakness
Prolonged sling use → stiffness; chronic massive tear → cuff arthropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rotator cuff/scapular strengthening, ergonomic changes, gradual return to overhead activity
Early supervised motion after injury when safe; avoid unnecessary immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: dermatomal symptoms, neck-provoked pain
ACS: exertional referred discomfort, diaphoresis, no motion-dependent localization
Pancoast tumor: smoking, hand weakness, Horner syndrome

table.title: Localizing examination
rows: Painful arc; positive Hawkins/Neer; strength preserved
Drop-arm or lag; objective resisted-movement weakness
Both active/passive motion limited, especially external rotation
Flattened deltoid; arm abducted, externally rotated
Anterior groove tenderness; pain with resisted supination

shoulder-pain.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAOS rotator cuff guideline 2025](https://www.aaos.org/quality/quality-programs/rotator-cuff/); other examination patterns established teaching.

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia → encapsulated infection from early childhood; **S. pneumoniae** leads pneumonia and fulminant sepsis

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival
Acute chest trigger: **infection** most common; in situ thrombosis and fat embolism less often
Severe anemia → low viscosity, vasodilation, ↓afterload → **↑cardiac output** preserves oxygen delivery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → prompt **IV opioid**, morphine (AKI: lower dose or hydromorphone); no meperidine; NSAID only if kidneys normal
Pain crisis support: euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia; no routine transfusion
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe acute chest, stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**; sequestration (cautious) or aplasia → simple transfusion
Fever → immediate **IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime**, despite daily penicillin prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia
Chronic hemolysis → ↑folate demand → **folate deficiency**, macrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

stridor.name: Stridor
stridor.scope: Laryngomalacia (inspiratory, worse supine), tracheomalacia (expiratory), vocal cord dysfunction (paradoxical adduction), vascular ring (biphasic, dysphagia), flexible laryngoscopy
stridor.core: Harsh upper-airway noise: respiratory phase localizes obstruction; age, feeding difficulty, and episodic triggers identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Congenital airway abnormalities in infancy; prematurity, prior intubation, tracheoesophageal fistula → tracheal weakness
Exercise, stress, irritants → inducible laryngeal obstruction; aortic arch anomalies → extrinsic compression

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Retractions, cyanosis, apnea, exhaustion, or poor air movement** → impending respiratory failure
Feeding-associated choking, recurrent pneumonia, or poor growth → clinically significant obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inspiratory: extrathoracic collapse; expiratory: intrathoracic collapse; biphasic: fixed central obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable unexplained upper-airway noise → **awake flexible laryngoscopy**
Dynamic bronchoscopy assesses distal collapse; CT angiography/MR angiography delineates vascular compression
Normal examination between episodes does not exclude inducible obstruction; visualize during symptoms/exercise
Flow-volume loop: flattened inspiratory limb supports variable extrathoracic obstruction; not definitive alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Distress → oxygen, minimize agitation, **urgent controlled airway** with anesthesia/ENT
Mild congenital malacia → observation, feeding assessment, upright feeding while awake; spontaneous improvement with growth
★ Severe laryngeal collapse with apnea/poor growth → **supraglottoplasty**
Severe tracheal collapse → CPAP; refractory disease → airway surgery
Inducible obstruction → speech-guided breathing; symptomatic vascular ring → surgical division

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxemia, aspiration, recurrent respiratory infections, growth failure; severe obstruction → arrest
Misdiagnosed inducible obstruction → unnecessary bronchodilators, glucocorticoids, or intubations

rows.label: Prevention
items: Supine sleep on flat surface despite positional noise; no prone sleeping or wedges
Avoid smoke exposure; swallowing assessment and feeding modifications reduce aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Croup: acute barky cough after URI; responds to dexamethasone
Foreign body: abrupt choking; rigid bronchoscopy despite normal radiograph
Epiglottitis: fever, drooling, tripod posture; avoid upsetting child or bedside throat examination

table.title: Chronic or episodic causes
rows: Expiratory; barking cough, worsens with exertion
Biphasic wheeze, dysphagia; steroid-unresponsive; neck extension relieves

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

subarachnoid-hemorrhage.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.scope: Ruptured saccular aneurysm, thunderclap headache, noncontrast head CT, lumbar puncture and xanthochromia, nimodipine, complications
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.core: Sudden headache maximal within seconds, often during exertion, with possible meningismus or collapse: presume subarachnoid hemorrhage until excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, hypertension, family history, prior aneurysm; autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
**Saccular aneurysm rupture**: most common nontraumatic cause, exceeds AVM; circle-of-Willis branch points; cocaine ↑ risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, transient loss of consciousness; sentinel headache may precede major hemorrhage
★ **Painful pupil-involving CN III palsy** → posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Sudden stupor, focal deficits, Cushing response, seizures → raised ICP/herniation; normal exam does not exclude hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Blood enters subarachnoid space → meningeal irritation, ↑ICP, impaired CSF resorption
Blood-breakdown products and vascular injury contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT immediately**: hyperdense basal cisterns/sulci; sensitivity declines with elapsed time
★ Negative CT >6 hours after onset or neurologic deficit → **LP**, assessing xanthochromia and RBCs
High-quality CT within 6 hours, neurologically intact, expert interpretation → may exclude SAH without routine LP
Confirmed blood → **CT angiography**; negative/inconclusive CTA with suspected aneurysm → catheter angiography
Traumatic tap may show falling RBCs; clearing alone cannot reliably exclude SAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Support airway, reverse anticoagulation, analgesia; severe hypertension → IV nicardipine; avoid hypotension/BP swings
★ **Urgent aneurysm coiling or clipping**, preferably within 24 hours, prevents rebleeding
★ **Enteral nimodipine for 21 days**, maintain euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia
Acute symptomatic hydrocephalus → external ventricular drainage
Secured aneurysm + delayed ischemia → induced hypertension; refractory → endovascular vasodilator/angioplasty

rows.label: Complications
items: Early rebleeding, hydrocephalus, seizures; delayed ischemia typically days 3–14
Hyponatremia from SIADH or cerebral salt wasting; stress cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema
ACom aneurysm rupture/clipping → **frontal lobe injury**: abulia, apathy, reduced spontaneous speech without depressed mood

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and BP control; specialist screening discussion for ≥2 affected first-degree relatives or high-risk ADPKD

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction: recurrent thunderclap headaches; segmental angiographic narrowing
Meningitis: fever and inflammatory CSF rather than aneurysmal bleeding
Migraine: usually slower onset, recurrent stereotyped episodes; first thunderclap still needs hemorrhage evaluation

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

supraventricular-tachycardia.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
supraventricular-tachycardia.scope: AVNRT, AVRT, focal atrial tachycardia, vagal maneuvers, adenosine, synchronized cardioversion, catheter ablation
supraventricular-tachycardia.core: Abrupt rapid regular palpitations with a usually narrow QRS often represent AV-node-dependent reentry; stability determines immediate electrical versus pharmacologic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Accessory pathway, prior episodes, adrenergic triggers, caffeine/stimulants
Focal atrial tachycardia may accompany structural disease; incessant forms can cause cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Regular rate often 150–250/min; palpitations, lightheadedness, dyspnea, neck pounding
★ **Hypotension, shock, ischemic chest pain, altered mentation**, or acute HF → unstable tachycardia
WPW between episodes: short PR, delta wave, widened QRS; may be absent with concealed pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reentry requires distinct conduction/refractory properties; AV node participates in AVNRT and orthodromic AVRT
Adenosine transiently blocks AV conduction; automatic atrial rhythms may continue despite transient ventricular slowing

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **12-lead ECG during episode**, continuous rhythm monitoring; check electrolytes, medication/exposure triggers
Wide-complex rhythm uncertain → presume VT rather than casually applying narrow-complex algorithm
Structural concern → echocardiography; recurrent undocumented events → ambulatory monitoring/electrophysiology evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; sedation if feasible without delaying rescue
★ Stable regular narrow rhythm → **modified Valsalva → rapid IV adenosine**
Persistent stable SVT → IV diltiazem/verapamil or beta blocker if no contraindication; cardioversion if unsuccessful
★ Irregular wide preexcited AF → **procainamide or cardioversion**; avoid AV-nodal blockers, including adenosine
Recurrent symptomatic AVNRT/AVRT or focal tachycardia → catheter ablation; selected patients use oral nodal blockers

rows.label: Complications
items: Syncope, demand ischemia, tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; preexcited AF can degenerate to VF
Adenosine: brief flushing/chest pressure, bronchospasm; avoid in active severe bronchospasm

rows.label: Prevention
items: Teach vagal maneuver, limit personal triggers; discuss definitive ablation for recurrence
Ablation near AV node carries small heart-block risk; shared procedural decision

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sinus tachycardia: gradual rate changes, beat-to-beat variability, physiologic driver; infants rarely >220/min
Atrial flutter: atrial sawtooth waves, often ventricular rate near 150

supraventricular-tachycardia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AHA adult advanced life support](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/cpr-and-ecc-guidelines/adult-advanced-life-support), [ACC/AHA AF guideline (2023)](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2023.08.017).

surgical-wound-complications.name: Surgical wound complications
surgical-wound-complications.scope: Superficial wound separation, fascial dehiscence (profuse serosanguineous drainage, emergent reclosure), evisceration (sterile saline dressings, emergency surgery), wound hematoma, wound seroma, surgical site infection
surgical-wound-complications.core: Postoperative wound drainage or separation requires determining whether fascia is intact; fascial failure is a surgical emergency even without exposed bowel.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, diabetes, malnutrition, smoking, glucocorticoids, wound infection, emergency/contaminated surgery
Vomiting, coughing, ileus or strenuous activity increase abdominal pressure on healing closure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Sudden profuse serosanguineous drainage**, popping sensation, or new bulge → suspect deep disruption
Erythema, warmth, worsening pain, purulence → infection; systemic toxicity may precede visible skin changes
★ Pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae, rapid progression → **necrotizing infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Early wound tensile strength depends on sutures; collagen remodeling later restores tissue support
Dead space permits fluid/blood accumulation; infection and poor perfusion impair collagen deposition

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Inspect/probe separated incision gently using sterile technique to assess **fascial integrity**
CBC, culture purulent drainage; systemic illness → blood cultures/lactate
Uncertain deep collection, stable patient → ultrasound/CT; obvious emergency → surgery without imaging delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Evisceration: sterile saline-moistened dressing**, supine, NPO, IV fluids, antibiotics, emergency operating room
Never force exposed bowel back through wound; surgical exploration determines viability and closure
Cellulitis alone → cefazolin/cephalexin; purulence → drainage, add antibiotics for cellulitis/systemic illness
Polymicrobial deep infection → piperacillin-tazobactam; add vancomycin for MRSA risk
Necrotizing infection → immediate debridement + broad IV antibiotics; antibiotics alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, sepsis, bowel ischemia, incisional hernia; delayed healing and recurrent separation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile technique, glucose control, smoking cessation, adequate protein/calories

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contact dermatitis: pruritic geometric rash matching adhesive, no purulent drainage
Normal healing ridge: firm linear swelling without progressive pain, erythema, or systemic illness

table.title: Stable localized findings
rows: Observe; aspirate/drain if symptomatic or persistent
Small stable: observe; expanding: evacuate, control bleeding
Open/drain if needed, dressings, secondary closure/healing

surgical-wound-complications.evidence: Not checked online; established postoperative wound and emergency surgical management.

sympathomimetic-toxicity.name: Sympathomimetic toxicity
sympathomimetic-toxicity.scope: Cocaine, amphetamines, methamphetamine, sympathomimetic toxidrome, benzodiazepines, cooling, avoidance of pure beta-blockers
sympathomimetic-toxicity.core: Stimulant exposure produces agitation, diaphoresis, mydriasis, hypertension, tachycardia, and hyperthermia; sedation limits dangerous catecholamine excess.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cocaine, amphetamines, methamphetamine, synthetic cathinones; prescription stimulant misuse
Coingested alcohol forms cocaethylene with cocaine, increasing cardiotoxicity; exertion/heat worsens injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Paranoia, psychosis, seizures, chest pain; bowel sounds usually active
★ **Severe hyperthermia, acidosis, rigidity/agitation, arrhythmia** → life-threatening poisoning
Cocaine additionally blocks sodium channels, producing QRS widening
MDMA: bruxism, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, severe **hyponatremia** from water intake and SIADH

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cocaine inhibits monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release → adrenergic/dopaminergic overstimulation
Vasoconstriction, increased oxygen demand, platelet activation → myocardial/cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical toxidrome**; temperature, glucose, ECG, electrolytes, creatinine, CK, urinalysis
Chest pain → serial ECG/troponin; neurologic deficit/severe headache → head CT for hemorrhage/stroke
Urine immunoassay supports exposure but false positives/negatives occur; never delay stabilization for results

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Benzodiazepines first** for agitation, seizures, tachycardia, hypertension; airway support when necessary
★ **Rapid external cooling + IV crystalloids** for hyperthermia/rhabdomyolysis; antipyretics ineffective
Persistent severe hypertension/vasospasm → nitroglycerin, nicardipine, or phentolamine after sedation
★ Acute cocaine toxicity: **avoid pure beta-blocker monotherapy**; unopposed alpha vasoconstriction concern
Wide QRS ventricular toxicity → sodium bicarbonate; ACS evaluation and aspirin when bleeding contraindications absent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, aortic dissection, ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, seizures, rhabdomyolysis, AKI, DIC
Methamphetamine: formication, dental decay, psychosis, cardiomyopathy; cocaine snorting: rhinitis, septal perforation; pregnancy: abruption

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer addiction treatment and contingency management; assess depression and suicidality after stimulant crash
Harm-reduction counseling, avoid mixing substances; naloxone access for possible opioid contamination

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anticholinergic toxicity: dry skin, urinary retention, reduced bowel sounds
Serotonin syndrome: inducible/spontaneous clonus, hyperreflexia; NMS: dopamine blockade, lead-pipe rigidity
Thyroid storm: thyroid disease with sustained systemic hypermetabolism
PCP: rotatory/vertical nystagmus, violent agitation; also sedate with benzodiazepines

systemic-lupus-erythematosus.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.scope: Diagnostic criteria (serositis, arthritis, lupus nephritis), neonatal lupus (congenital AV block), autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), pharmacotherapy (hydroxychloroquine, glucocorticoids)
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.core: Multisystem autoimmunity combining inflammatory joint, skin, serosal, renal, hematologic, or neurologic disease; flares often lower complement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive-age women; family history; UV exposure, infections, estrogen-related triggers

rows.label: Clues
items: Photosensitive malar rash sparing nasolabial folds; painless oral ulcers; nonscarring alopecia
Symmetric nonerosive arthritis, pleuritic pain, pericarditis; leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hemolysis
★ **Proteinuria, RBC casts**, edema or hypertension → renal involvement
Neonatal lupus: maternal anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB; congenital AV block may be permanent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-complex deposition activates **classical complement**, consuming C3/C4; autoantibody-mediated blood-cell destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANA** sensitive entry test; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm more specific
Anti-dsDNA titers, C3/C4, CBC, urinalysis, urine protein/creatinine, creatinine assess activity
★ Proteinuria **>0.5 g/g** or unexplained renal dysfunction → kidney biopsy
Classification: ANA ≥1:80, weighted score ≥10 with clinical criterion; clinical diagnosis remains contextual

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydroxychloroquine** broadly; NSAIDs for mild arthritis/serositis, glucocorticoids for flares
Organ-threatening flare → IV methylprednisolone; nephritis → mycophenolate plus belimumab/calcineurin inhibitor
Cyclophosphamide alternative for severe renal/CNS disease; taper glucocorticoids after disease control
Pregnancy → continue hydroxychloroquine; avoid mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Complications
items: Accelerated atherosclerosis, infection, CKD; antiphospholipid antibodies → thrombosis or pregnancy loss
Hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity; chronic steroid osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Sun protection; vaccines, cardiovascular risk control, retinal monitoring
Plan pregnancy during quiescence; anti-Ro/La positivity → fetal cardiac surveillance discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced lupus: antihistone antibodies, usually no renal/CNS disease
Rheumatoid arthritis: erosions; fibromyalgia: pain without inflammatory findings

thoracic-trauma.name: Thoracic trauma
thoracic-trauma.scope: Blunt and penetrating chest trauma, blunt cardiac injury, blunt aortic injury, diaphragmatic rupture, pulmonary contusion
thoracic-trauma.core: Chest trauma with respiratory or circulatory compromise requires immediate treatment of life-threatening injuries before definitive imaging.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, steering-wheel impact, crush injuries, penetrating wounds
Lower chest wounds can cross diaphragm and injure abdominal organs

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral absent breath sounds, shock, distended neck veins → tension pneumothorax
Flail segment: paradoxical movement; associated lung injury drives hypoxemia
Hypoxemia hours after impact + focal alveolar infiltrate, worsening to 24–48 h, afebrile → **pulmonary contusion**
Left thoracic bowel sounds/loops, **NG tip in left chest**, obscured hemidiaphragm → diaphragmatic rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pleural pressure or pericardial blood impairs venous return → obstructive shock
Alveolar hemorrhage and edema impair gas exchange; rapid deceleration shears the aortic isthmus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Primary survey with **eFAST** and portable chest radiograph; unstable injuries treated clinically
★ Deceleration + **widened mediastinum** → aortic injury; stable → **CT angiography**; normal radiograph cannot exclude
Blunt cardiac injury → ECG and troponin; both normal effectively exclude significant injury
Sternal/anterior rib fractures + new arrhythmia/↑troponin → telemetry; persistent shock → echocardiography
Large persistent air leak, subcutaneous air despite working chest tube → **tracheobronchial rupture**; bronchoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension pneumothorax → immediate needle/finger decompression → **chest tube**; no imaging delay
Open pneumothorax → vented seal and tube; hemothorax → tube and blood resuscitation
★ Initial tube blood >1500 mL or persistent >200 mL/h → operative exploration
Tamponade with shock/arrest → surgical drainage; pericardiocentesis only temporizing
Contusion/flail chest → oxygen, regional/multimodal analgesia, pulmonary hygiene; intubate for respiratory failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Contusion → ARDS; retained hemothorax → empyema
Rib fractures → splinting, atelectasis, pneumonia; cardiac injury → arrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seat belts, vehicle safety systems and protective equipment reduce injury risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myocardial contusion: ventricular ectopy, rising wedge pressure, pulmonary edema after fluids; no pericardial compression
Abdominal hemorrhage: free intraperitoneal fluid; may coexist with thoracic injury
Massive hemothorax: **opacified hemithorax**, flat neck veins; tension pneumothorax: hyperlucent
ARDS: bilateral opacities after 24–48 h; fat embolism: long-bone fracture, petechiae, confusion

thoracic-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established ATLS-based teaching.

table.title: Definitive associated-injury management
rows: IV esmolol if tolerated; endovascular repair

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG platelet clearance, impaired megakaryocytes; maternal IgG crosses placenta → **fetal platelet destruction**
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT: anti-PF4/heparin IgG activates platelets, producing thrombosis
**Kasabach-Merritt**: infant vascular tumor (kaposiform hemangioendothelioma/tufted angioma; older exams: hemangioma) traps platelets → severe thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.name: Thyroid nodules and cancer
thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.scope: Evaluation (TSH, ultrasound, FNA), benign goiter (multinodular goiter, compressive symptoms), thyroid cancer types
thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.core: A thyroid nodule requires functional assessment and ultrasound risk stratification; suspicious nonfunctioning nodules require cytologic evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childhood head/neck irradiation, familial thyroid cancer, MEN 2
Multinodular goiter: iodine deficiency, age; multiple nodules do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Hard fixed lesion, cervical nodes, rapid growth or persistent hoarseness increase cancer concern
Large benign goiter → dysphagia, positional dyspnea, tracheal compression
Anaplastic cancer: older adult with rapidly enlarging invasive neck mass

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Follicular-derived tumors differ in differentiation and spread; C-cell tumors produce calcitonin
Autonomous nodules synthesize hormone without pituitary stimulation and rarely contain malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable nodule → **TSH and thyroid ultrasound** first; document cervical nodes and suspicious features
★ Low TSH → radionuclide scan; hot nodule generally **no FNA**
Normal/high TSH → ultrasound-guided FNA by sonographic risk and size
High/intermediate suspicion ≥1 cm → FNA; low suspicion ≥1.5 cm; very low suspicion ≥2 cm
★ Follicular neoplasm on FNA → diagnostic lobectomy; **capsular/vascular invasion** requires histology

rows.label: Tx
items: Benign asymptomatic nodule → ultrasound follow-up; compressive or substernal goiter → surgery
Differentiated cancer → lobectomy/thyroidectomy by risk; selected higher-risk cases → radioactive iodine
★ Medullary cancer → thyroidectomy; evaluate **pheochromocytoma before surgery**
Anaplastic disease → airway planning, multidisciplinary systemic/local treatment; radioiodine ineffective

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury → hoarseness; bilateral injury → airway obstruction
Post-thyroidectomy hypoparathyroidism → hypocalcemia; expanding hematoma → emergency decompression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary neck radiation; RET-positive families → counseling and preventive thyroidectomy planning
Asymptomatic adult: **no routine ultrasound**; USPSTF against average-risk screening; older questions may expect palpation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Thyroiditis: tenderness or inflammatory history, transient dysfunction
Thyroglossal cyst: midline mass moves with tongue protrusion

table.title: Cancer signatures
rows: Orphan Annie nuclei; psammoma bodies; lymphatic spread

thyroid-nodules-and-cancer.evidence: Not checked online; established ATA nodule evaluation and board-level management.

transfusion-reactions.name: Transfusion reactions
transfusion-reactions.scope: Acute hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, TRALI, TACO, anaphylactic, delayed hemolytic, massive transfusion complications
transfusion-reactions.core: New symptoms during transfusion require stopping the transfusion immediately and evaluating hemolysis, infection and cardiopulmonary compromise.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior transfusion/pregnancy → alloantibodies; IgA deficiency with anti-IgA → anaphylaxis
Heart/kidney failure, rapid infusion, older age → circulatory overload

rows.label: Clues
items: Delayed hemolysis: hemoglobin falls, jaundice days–weeks after compatible transfusion; **DAT positive**, ↑indirect bilirubin
Bacterial contamination: high fever, rigors, profound hypotension; platelets particularly vulnerable
Isolated urticaria without systemic symptoms suggests mild allergic reaction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ABO mismatch → **preformed antibodies** → intravascular complement lysis; anamnestic → delayed extravascular hemolysis
TRALI: inflammatory pulmonary capillary leak; TACO: hydrostatic pressure from excess circulating volume
Febrile nonhemolytic: **cytokines accumulated in stored donor blood**; recipient anti-leukocyte antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Keep IV access with saline; **recheck patient/unit identity**, notify blood bank
Hemolysis: **DAT** shows coated RBCs; LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin; send unit/blood samples
Fever/shock → patient and product cultures; dyspnea → chest radiograph, oxygenation, volume assessment
Suspected febrile nonhemolytic reaction remains diagnosis of exclusion after hemolysis/sepsis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute hemolysis → IV saline, support renal perfusion, treat shock/DIC; **never restart unit**
★ Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine**, airway support; future washed or IgA-deficient products
TRALI → supportive oxygen/ventilation; diuretics generally unhelpful unless concomitant overload
TACO → upright positioning, oxygen, **IV furosemide**; slow future transfusions
Contamination → broad IV antibiotics; isolated allergy → diphenhydramine; febrile nonhemolytic → **acetaminophen**

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute hemolysis → AKI, DIC; severe pulmonary reactions → respiratory failure
Massive transfusion → citrate hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, dilutional thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bedside identification and crossmatch; leukoreduction reduces febrile reactions
Massive hemorrhage → balanced blood components, temperature and ionized calcium monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Underlying sepsis: symptoms may precede infusion; cultures clarify
Aspiration: event-linked infiltrate without transfusion-specific mechanism

transfusion-reactions.evidence: Not checked online; established transfusion-medicine definitions.

trauma-in-pregnancy.name: Trauma in pregnancy
trauma-in-pregnancy.scope: Maternal resuscitation priority, left uterine displacement, indicated diagnostic imaging, fetal monitoring, placental abruption detection, anti-D immune globulin, perimortem cesarean
trauma-in-pregnancy.core: Maternal stabilization comes first after trauma because fetal survival depends on maternal oxygenation and perfusion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Motor vehicle crash, falls, assault including intimate partner violence; direct abdominal impact or deceleration

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Uterine tenderness, contractions, vaginal bleeding or nonreassuring fetal tracing → suspect **abruption**
Pregnancy can mask substantial blood loss before maternal hypotension; external bleeding may be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gravid uterus compresses inferior vena cava supine, reducing preload; deceleration shears placental attachment

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Obtain indicated radiographs or CT; do not withhold necessary imaging because of pregnancy
★ Viable gestation after primary survey → continuous fetal and contraction monitoring for ≥4–6 hours
Contractions, bleeding, tenderness, serious injury or abnormal tracing → prolonged observation, commonly ≥24 hours
Ultrasound assesses viability and placenta; normal scan does not exclude abruption
Type and screen; Kleihauer–Betke testing in Rh-negative patients to guide additional RhIG

rows.label: Tx
items: Trauma ABCs, hemorrhage control, IV access and blood products when needed
★ Fundus at or above umbilicus → **manual left uterine displacement**, especially during supine CPR
Unsensitized Rh-negative with potentially sensitizing trauma → anti-D immune globulin within 72 hours
★ Arrest with fundus ≥umbilicus → prepare **resuscitative delivery** immediately; aim for delivery by 5 minutes

rows.label: Complications
items: Fetomaternal hemorrhage, preterm labor, fetal demise, uterine rupture, maternal coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Three-point restraint: lap belt below abdomen over hips, shoulder belt between breasts

rows.label: Mimics
items: Placenta previa: typically painless bleeding with placenta over internal os
Uterine rupture: abrupt pain, loss of fetal station or palpable fetal parts

trauma-in-pregnancy.evidence: Checked EAST pregnancy trauma and AHA resuscitation guidelines (2025).

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
tuberculosis.scope: Latent TB infection screening (PPD, IGRA), treatment regimens, active pulmonary TB, acid-fast bacilli smear and culture, RIPE therapy, extrapulmonary TB (Pott disease)
tuberculosis.core: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, and upper-lobe cavitation suggest contagious pulmonary tuberculosis; latent infection has no active disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Close contact, endemic residence, incarceration, homelessness, crowding, **long-term care** work/volunteering
HIV, TNF inhibitors, transplant, silicosis, diabetes → progression/reactivation risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Hemoptysis, prolonged fever; primary disease may cause hilar adenopathy or pleural effusion
★ **Back pain with vertebral destruction** → Pott disease; miliary spread causes diffuse micronodules
Tuberculous pleurisy: **lymphocytic exudate**, high protein, low glucose

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airborne bacilli survive in macrophages; T-cell granulomas contain infection; T-cell dysfunction → reactivation, skin-test anergy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screening: **IGRA** preferred after BCG; TST read induration at 48–72 hours
Positive screening → symptoms + chest radiograph; neither test distinguishes latent from active infection
★ Active suspicion → **sputum NAAT, AFB smear, culture and susceptibility**; collect serial specimens
Negative smear, TST or IGRA does not exclude active TB, especially with immunosuppression or malnutrition
Pott suspicion → spinal MRI, biopsy/culture; assess cord compression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected contagious disease → **airborne isolation** and public-health notification
Drug-susceptible active TB: 2 months isoniazid/rifampin/pyrazinamide/ethambutol → 4 months isoniazid/rifampin
Eligible pulmonary cases ≥12 years: 4-month isoniazid/rifapentine/moxifloxacin/pyrazinamide-based regimen alternative
Latent, no RIPE: 3-month isoniazid/rifapentine or 4-month rifampin; older questions may expect **isoniazid** alone, still acceptable
Isoniazid → pyridoxine prevents neuropathy, sideroblastic anemia; Pott with deficit/instability → urgent spinal surgery evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Meningitis, adrenal destruction, spinal cord compression, bronchiectasis
INH/rifampin/pyrazinamide: hepatotoxicity; ethambutol: optic neuropathy; rifampin: enzyme induction, orange secretions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Contact investigation**, latent-treatment completion; directly observed active treatment improves adherence
Review drug interactions and baseline liver risk; monitor visual acuity/color vision with ethambutol

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung cancer: focal malignant biopsy
Fungal infection: geographic exposure; nontuberculous mycobacteria: species identification distinguishes

table.title: Positive TST thresholds
rows: HIV, close contacts, transplant, substantial immunosuppression
Healthcare workers, exposure-risk groups, comorbidities, young children

tumor-lysis-syndrome.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
tumor-lysis-syndrome.scope: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, acute kidney injury, allopurinol, rasburicase, aggressive hydration
tumor-lysis-syndrome.core: Rapid malignant-cell destruction causes an electrolyte and urate emergency; anticipate risk before cancer treatment and respond immediately to evolving organ dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Burkitt/high-grade lymphoma, acute leukemia, bulky chemosensitive tumors, high LDH or leukocyte count
Renal impairment, dehydration, high baseline urate; cytotoxics, steroids, targeted drugs; sometimes spontaneous

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, weakness, muscle cramps, paresthesias or tetany shortly after treatment
★ **Oliguria, arrhythmia, seizure** signal clinical disease; abnormalities may precede symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intracellular potassium/phosphate and nucleic acids released; purine breakdown produces uric acid
Urate and calcium-phosphate precipitation injure kidneys; phosphate binding reduces serum calcium

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Check **K, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine**, LDH; ECG and continuous telemetry
Laboratory TLS: ≥2 abnormalities within 24 hours, from 3 days pretreatment through 7 days posttreatment
Clinical TLS: laboratory pattern plus AKI, arrhythmia/sudden death, or seizure
High-risk/established disease → repeat electrolytes and renal indices every 4–6 hours; strict intake/output

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic saline**, individualized to cardiac/renal status; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids
★ Dangerous hyperkalemia → **IV calcium for ECG changes**, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory abnormalities
Established hyperuricemia/high-risk TLS → rasburicase; screen **G6PD**, contraindicated if deficient
Phosphate restriction/binders; avoid treating asymptomatic hypocalcemia; symptomatic tetany/seizures → cautious calcium
Urgent dialysis: refractory K/phosphate, acidosis, symptomatic hypocalcemia, fluid overload, or worsening oliguric AKI

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute renal failure, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia, seizures, sudden death
Rasburicase → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; allopurinol → hypersensitivity and xanthine crystal burden

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Risk-stratify before treatment; **allopurinol + hydration** for intermediate risk; rasburicase for high risk
Allopurinol prevents new urate formation; does not remove existing uric acid
Avoid urinary alkalinization → calcium-phosphate precipitation; no routine concurrent allopurinol and rasburicase

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rhabdomyolysis: markedly elevated CK and myoglobinuria, muscle injury context
Isolated AKI: electrolyte retention without abrupt tumor-destruction pattern
Sepsis: infection-associated organ dysfunction; can coexist and trigger tumor lysis

tympanic-membrane-perforation.name: Tympanic membrane perforation
tympanic-membrane-perforation.scope: Traumatic perforation, blast injury, barotrauma, secondary infection, hearing loss, management
tympanic-membrane-perforation.core: Sudden ear pain followed by bleeding, hearing reduction or tinnitus after trauma or pressure change; most uncomplicated perforations heal with dry-ear precautions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cotton swabs/ear instrumentation, slap/blast, head trauma; diving or air travel with impaired pressure equalization
Otitis media can cause spontaneous rupture; contaminated water entry increases secondary infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Visible membrane defect, bloody otorrhea; conductive loss usually exceeds pain after initial event
★ **Severe vertigo, sensorineural loss, facial weakness** → inner-ear, ossicular or temporal-bone injury
Purulent discharge or increasing pain after contamination suggests superimposed infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Membrane disruption reduces sound transmission; persistent major loss may indicate ossicular chain discontinuity
Middle-ear exposure to water/bacteria predisposes to infection; healing requires epithelial migration across defect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Gentle otoscopy** confirms defect; avoid irrigation and pneumatic pressure with suspected acute perforation
Weber lateralizes toward affected ear in conductive loss; Rinne may show bone >air conduction
**Audiometry** quantifies loss; early testing for marked deficit; repeat after healing
Blast/head injury with neurologic signs → urgent ENT ± temporal-bone CT; assess for CSF leak

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clean uncomplicated injury → **observation, dry ear, analgesia**; antibiotics not routinely needed
Contamination or purulent otorrhea → **ofloxacin or ciprofloxacin ear drops**
★ Avoid **aminoglycoside drops**, alcohol/acidifying solutions, further instrumentation; potential ototoxicity or irritation
Large defect, major hearing deficit, ongoing vertigo or facial weakness → prompt ENT evaluation
Persistent defect around 2–3 months or ossicular disruption → ENT patching/tympanoplasty or reconstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic perforation, recurrent suppurative otitis media, persistent conductive loss
Associated labyrinthine injury → permanent sensorineural loss or vestibular symptoms; epithelial ingrowth → cholesteatoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Petrolatum-coated cotton at bathing**, no swimming until healed; avoid forceful nose blowing
Avoid inserting objects into ear; pressure equalization during descent, avoid diving with congestion
Follow-up examination and hearing assessment confirm closure and identify residual deficit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis externa: canal edema and tragal tenderness; membrane may be intact
Hemotympanum: blood behind intact membrane, often after trauma
Acute otitis media rupture: preceding fever/earache with bulging infected membrane, pain relief after drainage

tympanic-membrane-perforation.evidence: Antibiotic/referral decisions checked 2026-10-30: [CMAJ traumatic perforation review, 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10833100/).

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
